Role Description:

The Director, Procurement will facilitate ShipBob's strategic sourcing and procurement function across multiple categories. This is a senior leadership role responsible for developing and sustaining a high-performing procurement capability, driving meaningful cost improvement, and ensuring supplier relationships, contract frameworks, and category strategies are aligned with ShipBob's rapid growth trajectory. The Director brings deep commercial judgment, strong negotiation capability, and the ability to manage complexity across multiple categories simultaneously. Given the small size of the current team, the Director must be hands-on and highly adaptable including operating in the detail as readily as at the strategic level and flexing to changing priorities as the business evolves. This role manages the Procurement Manager and reports to the VP Global Controller.

What you’ll do:

As the senior leader responsible for procurement across ShipBob's global operations, you will have the following responsibilities:

  • Define and own ShipBob's procurement strategy across multiple categories, growing a function that is proactive, analytically rigorous, and commercially credible.
  • Manage and develop the procurement team, setting clear performance standards, operating frameworks, and a culture of data-oriented outcome.
  • Build and sustain executive-level relationships with strategic suppliers, ensuring ShipBob is positioned as an intelligent, sophisticated buyer across all categories.
  • Facilitate the most complex and commercially significant negotiations across ShipBob's supplier base in technology, facilities, and corporate services.
  • Design and execute structured RFx processes with full analytical rigor: market intelligence, benchmarking, scenario modelling, supplier assessment, and documented recommendation with supporting evidence.
  • Develop category strategies that are grounded in market data, total cost of ownership analysis, and ShipBob's operational requirements not historical spend patterns.
  • Build and maintain a vendor performance management framework with defined KPIs, governance cadence, and escalation protocols that hold suppliers accountable without creating adversarial relationships.
  • Review, redline, and negotiate contractual agreements across all categories ensuring favorable commercial terms, appropriate risk allocation, and long-term value protection.
  • Partner closely with Finance, Legal, Operations, and Technology to ensure procurement choices are integrated into ShipBob's planning and budget cycles.
  • Partner as needed with ShipBob's transportation and partner network procurement functions, coordinating across category boundaries while this role focuses on indirect, technology, facilities, corporate, and professional services spend.
  • Drive procurement process scalability, building systems, tools, and workflows that support ShipBob's growth without linear headcount growth in the function.
  • Facilitate change management initiatives required to implement process and structural improvements, including stakeholder alignment, communication, and adoption tracking. Central to this is driving a cultural shift as the function evolves — embedding discipline around compliance and rigorous review into how the organization buys, rather than optimizing for speed alone.
  • Ensure compliance with ShipBob's SOX, SOC II, and other regulatory requirements as they apply to the procurement function.
  • Use data analytics, industry benchmarking, and strategic sourcing methodologies to continuously identify and capture cost savings, risk reduction, and value-creation opportunities.
  • Additional duties and responsibilities as necessary.

What you’ll bring to the table:

  • Minimum 10 years of progressive procurement experience, with at least 3 years in a senior leadership role with direct management responsibility.
  • Proven track record leading strategic procurement across multiple categories, particularly technology/SaaS/AI, indirect, and professional services.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex, high-value negotiations with outcomes supported by documented market intelligence, benchmarking, and total cost analysis, not intuition alone.
  • Experience building or significantly upgrading a procurement function: establishing operating frameworks, performance standards, and team capability in a fast-growth environment, including leading the cultural shift toward compliance and disciplined review rather than speed alone.
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Finance, or related field; MBA or CPSM/CPM preferred.
  • High EQ and executive presence. Credible at the CFO and SVP level, able to translate complex commercial situations into clear recommendations and influence choices without direct authority.
  • Analytically rigorous. Every recommendation is supported by data, benchmarking, and documented study. Presenting a deal as 'good' without supporting evidence is not a standard this leader operates to.
  • Strong problem-solving and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple high-priority workstreams simultaneously in a complex, rapidly changing environment.
  • Hands-on and adaptable. Comfortable rolling up sleeves and operating without a large support structure, flexing readily to changing priorities given the small team size.
  • Deep understanding of US market dynamics, contract structures, cost drivers, and supplier landscape across multiple categories.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Able to write a clear, well-structured recommendation memo as readily as running a negotiation room.
  • Ability to cover core US hours with availability for occasional international coordination.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; experience with P2P platforms such as ZipHQ preferred; comfort working with AI, data tools and BI platforms.

Perks & Benefits:

  • Medical, Dental, Vision & Basic Life Insurance
  • Paid Maternity/Parental Leave Program
  • Paid Holidays & Flexible Time Off Program
  • Paid Sick Leave
  • Wellness Days (1 day/quarter)
  • 401K Match
  • Comprehensive Benefits Package >>>
  • See Our High-Performing Culture >>>Check us out on Instagram (@lifeatshipbob)

ShipBob believes in transparency while providing a competitive total compensation package with a pay for performance approach. We are targeting a salary range of $180,000 - $215,000 for this role. The full base pay range for this position in our compensation architecture is $148,800 - $248,000. In addition to base salary, this role includes the opportunity to be eligible for participation in the Company's discretionary bonus plan based on Company's plans and in accordance with Company’s policies.

We recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. Diversity of experience and skills combined with passion is a key to innovation and excellence; therefore, we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply to our positions.

About You:

Building the world’s leading full-stack fulfillment platform is challenging work. The problems we solve are complex, the pace is fast, and the bar is high. That means ShipBob’s environment isn’t the right fit for everyone, and that’s okay. If you are ready to take ownership, push boundaries, and grow alongside a team that genuinely supports each other, we would love to hear from you.

Learn more about our core values and how we perform at a high level in our day-to-day work on our Culture page ().

About Us:

ShipBob is a leading global supply chain and fulfillment technology platform designed for SMB and Mid-Market ecommerce merchants to provide them access to best-in-class capabilities and to deliver a delightful shopper experience. Merchants can outsource their entire fulfillment operations, utilize ShipBob’s proprietary warehouse management system for in-house fulfillment, or take advantage of a hybrid solution across ShipBob’s dozens of fulfillment center network in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Europe, and Australia. ShipBob is backed by leading investors like Menlo Ventures, Bain Capital Ventures, Hyde Park Venture Partners, and SoftBank Vision Fund 2, and is one of the fastest-growing tech companies headquartered in Chicago.

At ShipBob, every full-time employee gets access to our best-in-class AI and productivity tools from Day 1 at no cost. This isn't a pilot or a perk for select teams. It's standard for everyone. We believe innovation isn't owned by one department. Whether you're in Talent, Operations, Finance, Engineering, or Customer Success, we expect you to ask: how can this be done better, faster, or smarter? These tools are our investment in your ability to find those answers.

We may use AI-powered tools during our interview process to support things like notetaking and organizing feedback so our teams can stay focused on getting to know you. These tools help create a more consistent and thoughtful experience. That said, every hiring decision is made by a human.

Team Description:

The Ads Marketplace team is a strategic growth engine for Reddit Ads. Our mission is to democratize high-performance advertising by enabling brands to achieve world-class results with minimal friction. To achieve this, we need an incredibly robust, scalable, and state-of-the-art Machine Learning infrastructure. The Ads ML Platform team is at the core of this mission, tasked with building the foundation that powers all of our content understanding, ad targeting, and ad ranking models. We are empowering our ML engineers and data scientists to move faster and build smarter.

The Role:

As the Staff Product Manager for the Ads ML Platform, you will hold significant ownership over the infrastructure and tools that make our ads marketplace intelligent. You will define the vision and build the roadmap for a platform that enables unparalleled engineering velocity and supports the most modern ML architectures.

You will be the bridge between complex ML systems and business outcomes. Whether it's integrating generative AI to increase developer productivity, establishing unified model-serving infrastructure, or optimizing GPU utilization, your work will directly accelerate how quickly and effectively we can ship highly-performant ad products. If you are passionate about the intersection of platform engineering and state-of-the-art ML research, this is the role for you.

Responsibilities

  • Define the Vision: Shape the long-term strategy and roadmap for Reddit’s Ads ML platform, ensuring we are adopting cutting-edge technologies (including Generative AI and LLM workflows) to stay ahead of the curve.
  • Accelerate Velocity: Build products and tooling that dramatically reduce friction for Machine Learning Engineers (MLEs) and Data Scientists, enabling them to train, deploy, and iterate on models faster than ever.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner deeply with Engineering, Data Science, and Ads Product teams to understand their constraints, prioritize platform initiatives, and deliver scalable infrastructure.
  • Drive Execution and Adoption: Own key performance indicators (KPIs) around platform reliability, latency, cost-efficiency, usage metrics, and developer productivity.
  • Stay Cutting-Edge: Keep your finger on the pulse of the broader ML ecosystem. Read the latest research papers, understand emerging architectures, and determine how they can be practically applied to Reddit’s Ads ML platform.
  • Distill pain points, translate to requirements: Conduct regular user research with MLEs in Ranking, Creative Effectiveness and Content Understanding to convert pain points (e.g., slow backfills, limited training speed, no way to quickly share features across models) into precise product requirements. Validate the needs and ensure they are tied into a broader vision for the org.

Minimum Qualifications:

jobs.description:
Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We are seeking a Senior Support Operations Lead to design, implement, and continuously improve complex member journeys across our support ecosystem, with warranty replacements serving as a key initial focus area. This role will turn high-friction operational pain points into scalable workflows, tooling requirements, and cross-functional programs that improve member experience, reduce operational risk, and raise execution quality across systems and teams.

This role is ideal for someone who is strong in customer journey design, root-cause analysis, project management, executive-ready communication, and cross-functional collaboration. They should be comfortable operating at the intersection of support operations, systems, analytics, policy, and process design.

What You Will Do:

Customer journey design and operational improvement

  • Map and improve end-to-end member journeys across complex support experiences, especially warranty replacements, by identifying friction points across intake, eligibility, decisioning, fulfillment, returns, and follow-up communication.
  • Translate operational pain points into clear future-state workflows, decision trees, requirements, and guardrails that improve consistency for both members and agents.
  • Partner with stakeholders across Member Experience, Product, Engineering, Fraud, Finance, Logistics, and related teams to align on journey design priorities and ensure solutions work across systems and markets.

Root-cause analysis, analytics, and insight generation

  • Lead root-cause analysis on recurring operational issues by pulling together signals across support tooling, transactional systems, logistics data, and reporting environments.
  • Investigate failure patterns such as automation drop-off, process exceptions, queue health issues, RA/SO quality problems, and country- or channel-specific breakdowns, then convert findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Define and monitor KPIs, dashboards, and experiment plans that measure impact on member effort, operational efficiency, quality, and risk.

Program and project management

  • Own cross-functional improvement initiatives from problem definition through rollout, including scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, and stakeholder alignment.
  • Help maintain and prioritize an improvement roadmap that balances quick wins with foundational investments in tooling, reporting, and process quality.
  • Support launch readiness for new workflows, policy changes, and tooling updates by coordinating communications, documenting decisions, and monitoring post-launch performance.

Executive communication and stakeholder alignment

  • Create executive-ready presentations, updates, and business cases that synthesize operational problems, supporting data, trade-offs, and recommended next steps.
  • Communicate clearly with senior leadership, frontline teams, and cross-functional partners, adapting the level of detail to the audience while keeping decisions grounded in evidence.

Documentation, enablement, and change management

  • Build concise SOPs, playbooks, training materials, and operational guidance that reflect how teams actually work and reduce over-reliance on tribal knowledge.
  • Partner with QA, training, and operations teams to identify recurring errors, improve adoption of new workflows, and ensure process changes stick over time.

Requirements
We would love to have you on our team if you have:

  • 8+ years experience in support operations, customer experience operations, process improvement, program management, or similar roles in a fast-moving environment.
  • Demonstrated strength in customer journey design and the ability to translate complex operational challenges into scalable workflows, routing logic, and support processes.
  • Strong root-cause analysis and analytical problem-solving skills, including comfort working across multiple data sources and using metrics to drive decisions.
  • Strong project management and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, align stakeholders, and move initiatives from idea to execution.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear, executive-ready narratives and influence cross-functional partners.
  • Experience writing and maintaining clear operational documentation, SOPs, or training materials that improve execution quality at scale.
  • A collaborative working style and the ability to partner effectively across support, product, engineering, fraud, finance, logistics, and analytics teams.
  • Comfort working with operational systems and tools such as CRM/case platforms, automation tooling, knowledge management, analytics/BI environments, and back-end order or logistics systems.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working on warranty, replacements, returns, fraud, or other complex post-purchase support journeys.
  • Familiarity with tools and systems such as Zendesk, NetSuite, Narvar, Darwin, conversational AI platforms, Tableau, Lovable, or similar operational and analytics tooling.
  • Experience supporting change management in high-volume support environments, including launches, process rollouts, or tooling transitions.

Benefits

At Oura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Oura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

This is a day shift position working remotely. Coders abstract data from the anesthesia record into the MD Cloud Practice Solutions platform, and may also work with other charge capture platforms, including Medaxion, PC7, as well as multiple facility EMR’s based on assigned location.

Experience coding for physicians, CRNA, CAA, NP, SRNA, and residents required. NCCI bundling, familiarity with LCD/NCD, and experience with CMS guidelines for coding required. jobs.description:
By joining Sedgwick, you'll be part of something truly meaningful. It’s what our 33,000 colleagues do every day for people around the world who are facing the unexpected. Newsweek Recognizes Sedgwick as America’s Greatest Workplaces National Top Companies

Certified as a Great Place to Work®

Fortune Best Workplaces in Financial Services & Insurance

Director Product Management - AI

ARE YOU AN IDEAL CANDIDATE?

We are looking for a strategic, customer-focused leader who embodies Sedgwick’s values of empathy, accountability, collaboration, innovation, growth, and inclusion. The ideal candidate is passionate about transforming enterprise data into measurable value through modern data products, AI-powered experiences, and secure, governed platforms that enable better decisions at scale.

PRIMARY PURPOSE:

The Director, Product Management – AI Enabled Enterprise Data Products is responsible for defining and executing the product strategy, roadmap, and business outcomes for Sedgwick’s enterprise AI-enabled data product portfolio.

This role owns a portfolio of strategic data products including:

  • Enterprise AI Analyst and conversational analytics platforms that allow users to ask natural language questions and receive trusted insights, visualizations, recommendations, and analysis.
  • Enterprise data sharing, data exchange, marketplace, semantic layer, data catalog, and self-service analytics capabilities.
  • AI-enabled operational decision support products and analytical applications.

The Director serves as the bridge between business strategy, data strategy, AI innovation, technology execution, governance, and client value realization. This role leads Product Managers and Product Owners while partnering with Data Engineering, Architecture, Security, Governance, AI Engineering, Analytics, and Business leaders to deliver secure, scalable, governed, and measurable enterprise capabilities.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Define Product Vision and Strategy

  • Define and own the multi-year vision, strategy, roadmap, business model, and investment priorities for enterprise AI and data products.
  • Establish a product portfolio that enables business users, clients, and operational teams to discover, access, share, and analyze trusted enterprise data.
  • Drive AI-powered analytical experiences that allow users to interact with enterprise data through natural language and conversational interfaces.
  • Partner with executive leadership to identify opportunities that improve decision-making, efficiency, client experience, revenue growth, and cost optimization.
  • Develop business cases, success measures, portfolio-level OKRs, and executive communications on progress, risks, and architectural implications.

Oversee, coordinate & support development work

  • Oversee delivery across multiple teams, ensuring alignment between product strategy, technical execution, architectural direction, and client outcomes.
  • Set expectations for backlog quality, acceptance criteria, prioritization, capacity planning, dependency management, and delivery risk mitigation.
  • Own product portfolio KPIs and contributions to Product Group and enterprise OKRs, including quality, efficiency, sustainability, and value delivery.
  • Ensure solutions comply with enterprise security, privacy, regulatory, governance, and responsible AI requirements.
  • Serve as the senior escalation point for product-related dependencies, risks, and prioritization conflicts.

Own Enterprise Data Product Portfolio

  • Establish product management practices for enterprise data products, including data-as-a-product principles.
  • Define and manage reusable, governed data products supporting claims, finance, compliance, operations, client, and executive reporting needs.
  • Drive adoption of semantic models, business glossaries, metadata, cataloging, and self-service analytics capabilities.
  • Lead product strategy for enterprise data-sharing solutions for internal consumers, clients, partners, and third-party integrations.
  • Ensure data products are reliable, scalable, discoverable, secure, usable, and supported by lineage and governance.

Drive AI Analyst and Conversational Analytics Capabilities

  • Own the product vision for AI-powered analytics that provide trusted answers, insights, metrics, visualizations, and recommendations through natural language interactions.
  • Partner with business teams to identify high-value analytical use cases and decision-support opportunities.
  • Define requirements for semantic layers, knowledge models, retrieval experiences, governance controls, trust mechanisms, and user experiences.
  • Measure AI product effectiveness through adoption, accuracy, user satisfaction, business impact, and operational efficiency.
  • Ensure AI-generated insights are explainable, governed, auditable, and aligned with enterprise policies.

Enable Secure Enterprise Data Sharing

  • Define strategy and roadmap for enterprise-scale data exchange and sharing capabilities.
  • Partner with Security, Governance, Privacy, and Legal teams to establish secure and compliant data-sharing frameworks.
  • Drive capabilities for role-based access, entitlements, auditing, lineage, masking, client access controls, and data-sharing agreements.
  • Enable governed data product distribution across business units, clients, partners, and external ecosystems while supporting growth, performance, compliance, and resilience.

Stakeholder Engagement and Value Realization

  • Build strong relationships with business leaders, claims operations, finance, client services, technology leaders, and external stakeholders.
  • Translate business objectives and operational challenges into actionable AI and data product strategies.
  • Communicate roadmap progress, risks, dependencies, investment needs, and outcomes to executive leadership.
  • Establish and monitor portfolio-level KPIs, OKRs, and value realization metrics that trace strategy through implementation to business impact.

People Leadership

  • Lead and develop Product Owners, Scrum Masters, and product delivery teams.
  • Establish product management best practices across AI, data, analytics, and platform teams.
  • Coach teams on customer-centric product development, Agile practices, outcome-based planning, and value measurement.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, experimentation, accountability, continuous learning, and collaboration.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Licensing

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Data Science, or related field required.
  • Master's degree preferred.

Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in Product Management, Data Products, Analytics Platforms, AI Products, or Enterprise Technology.
  • 5+ years leading Product Managers or Product Owners and managing product portfolios.
  • Experience owning enterprise-scale data, analytics, AI, platform, reporting, self-service analytics, semantic modeling, AI/ML, or conversational AI products.
  • Experience defining product strategy, roadmaps, business cases, and measurable outcomes for data-driven products.
  • Experience working in Agile or scaled Agile environments and leading cross-functional teams across Architecture, Data Engineering, Analytics, Security, Governance, and Business stakeholders.

Skills & Knowledge

  • Expert knowledge of Agile methodologies, product operating models, portfolio management, prioritization, roadmap development, and outcome measurement.
  • Ability to translate business and portfolio strategy into product vision, execution standards, and measurable value.
  • Deep understanding of Data as a Product principles, modern data platforms, data mesh, data fabric, governance, semantic modeling, metadata, lineage, and enterprise analytics architectures.
  • Strong understanding of AI, generative AI, conversational analytics, augmented decision-support platforms, and responsible AI practices.
  • Experience with enterprise data sharing, security, privacy, governance, compliance frameworks, and risk management.
  • Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, product adoption, organizational change, and people leadership capabilities.
  • Ability to balance business value, technical complexity, investment, risk, and operational impact.

Success Measures

The Director will be evaluated on:

  • Delivery of a clear enterprise AI and data product strategy, roadmap, and investment plan.
  • Adoption and measurable business value from AI-enabled analytics, data products, and data-sharing capabilities.
  • Improved data product quality, usability, discoverability, governance, security, and scalability.
  • Effective stakeholder alignment, executive communication, prioritization, and value realization.
  • Development of high-performing product teams and consistent product management practices.

  • Planejar, estruturar e gerir diretamente campanhas de mídia paga de alta complexidade (Search, Social, Display, App, entre outros).
  • Dominar operacionalmente bidding, segmentação, estrutura de contas, testes de criativos e funil de conversão.

  • Aplicar visões de mensuração avançada e modelos de atribuição no dia a dia da gestão de mídia.

2. Execução da Estratégia de Growth & Aquisição (B2C & B2B)

  • Propor realocações táticas de budget entre canais e campanhas com base na performance real e ROI incremental.

5. Interface com Agência, CRM, SEO e Produto

  • Acompanhar o dia a dia da agência parceira, garantindo qualidade, velocidade e precisão técnica nas entregas.
  • Atuar de forma integrada com os times de CRM e SEO para alinhar mensagens, jornada e maximizar a conversão orgânica e paga.
  • Interagir com times de Dados, Produto e Engenharia para garantir o bom funcionamento da infraestrutura de tracking, dados e melhorias no funil de aquisição.

Experiência:

  • Experiência sólida e prática na gestão de campanhas de alta complexidade e orçamentos expressivos em Mídia de Performance.
  • Experiência comprovada com estratégias de aquisição B2C e/ou B2B em ambientes digitais complexos (marketplaces, e-commerce, lead generation ou tech empresas).
  • Vivência na execução e acompanhamento de testes A/B, de incrementalidade ou mensuração de lift.

jobs.description:
Job Description - Account Manager

Reports To: Senior Director of Account Management

Department: Account Management

Location: Remote

Position Type: Full-Time

Position Summary

AxisCare is building a new Account Management function, and this Account Manager will join an early Account Management team with the opportunity to help build and shape the role and department. This role owns AxisCare's key accounts, not just executing contract renewals, but proactively growing net revenue retention (NRR) by identifying and offering strategic add-ons that increase monthly recurring revenue. The Account Manager will own an initiative to identify white space within strategic customer accounts, uncovering opportunities where the customer could benefit from additional add-on services and/or integrations at the time of renewal, and will engage solutions engineers across the relevant product lines, including RCM, payments, AI, data add-ons, and preferred partnerships, to support execution.

The ideal candidate will be able to plan strategically for their book of business as well as manage the detailed actions of account planning and contract negotiation. The Account Manager role will work as a partner with the CSM role. As an Account Manager you will be accountable for Net Revenue Retention and will be accountable for the client activities required to achieve strong NRR such as renewal management, expansion identification, opportunity qualification, scoping, negotiation, and handling off-cycle cancellation and renegotiation requests.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the commercial aspects of AxisCare's key accounts end-to-end, including contract renewals, pricing conversations, and strategic expansion  
  • Identify and execute opportunities to grow NRR  
  • Own opportunity management, become a subject matter expert on add-on opportunities, and coordinate with supporting resources as they become available (i.e. Solution Engineering, business unit SME’s, etc.) to bring those opportunities to closed won. 
  • Proactively manage renewal timelines; communicate renewal terms and pricing updates to customers 
  • Negotiate contract renewals, pricing increases, and amendments with professionalism and tact while reinforcing product value 
  • Serve as the owner for inbound cancellation and off-cycle renegotiation requests, leading save and retention efforts, coordinating with Customer Success and Finance, and documenting churn reasons and outcomes 
  • Partner with Sales Management and Legal to review non-standard terms and maintain consistent contract language 
  • Collaborate with Sales and Customer Success to ensure strong customer health, knowledge transfer, and the identification of expansion opportunities  
  • Provide contract and account-related reporting and insights to leadership 
  • Identify opportunities to improve contract workflows, renewal processes, and documentation accuracy 
  • Uphold compliance with internal controls, approval workflows, and data handling standards 
  • Provide insight to help refine contract templates and renewal communication processes 
  • As an early member of a growing Account Management team, help build and shape the processes, tools, and strategy for the function 
  • Own and report on key performance indicators, including: 
    • Net revenue retention (NRR) and Gross revenue retention (GRR) 
    • Add-on attach rate at renewal 
    • Renewal rate 
    • Bookings/contract adjustments from renewals 
    • Churn reasons 

What We're Looking For (Minimum Qualifications)

  • At least two years of experience in contract renewals
  • Highly skilled in the art of negotiation, with the thick skin needed to navigate pricing uplift conversations
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and keep customers satisfied while executing a price uplift
  • Strong organizational and multitasking abilities, with the ability to manage numerous accounts and contracts simultaneously
  • Collaborative, cross-functional mindset, comfortable working with Finance, Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineers, and legal counsel
  • Ability to analyze account and contract data to identify NRR growth opportunities
  • Experience with HubSpot preferred,

    ChurnZero a plus

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel

Working Conditions

  • Manual dexterity required to use desktop computer and peripherals.
  • Utilization of software and email to perform job functions.
  • Will need to conduct camera-on videoconferencing for customer calls.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.
  • Medical insurance premiums are covered in full for the employee (Medical, Dental and Vision) 
  • 401K with competitive company matching.
  • Personal time off, sick leave, and holidays.
  • Company will provide laptop and other needed computer equipment.

About AxisCare

According to Pew Research, roughly 10,000 baby boomers turn 65 every day, and the American Society on Aging calculated that an American has a 70% chance of needing help with activities of daily living such as dressing, bathing, hygiene, etc. This has led to an unprecedented increase in Home Care agencies in the U.S. and abroad who strive to help those who have difficulty helping themselves, specifically offering non-medical (also referred to as non-skilled) services to seniors in their homes.

AxisCare was started in 2011 by industry leaders to help meet the demand for a more userfriendly and mobile-compatible solution. Our product is a web-based management platform that helps agencies manage CRM and marketing, Caregiver/Client scheduling, billing, payroll and much more. Headquartered in Waco, TX, AxisCare has clients in all 50 states as well as 7 other countries. We are a fast-growing company seeking high-performing individuals looking for a fast-paced, autonomous working environment.

BIDDING INSTRUCTIONS

1. Bidding Instructions

1.1 Technical Proposal

Bidders shall include in the Technical Proposal:

1. A CV of the proposed candidate clearly indicating relevant experience for the stated requirements in Section 12 (Qualifications) of this Statement of Work (SoW).

2. A Compliance matrix referring to how each candidate meets the stated requirements as per Section 12 of this SoW, justified by relevant (project) experience.

Deadline Date: Monday 14 September 2026

Requirement: Intelligence Systems E-Learning / Micro Lesson / Wiki Development SME Support

Location: 100% Off-site at contractor's premises, with meetings at NATO premises as required.

Note: Please refer to your Subcontract Agreement, article 6.4.1.a, which states 'Off-Site Discount: 5% (this discount is applicable to all requirements, and applies when the assigned personnel are permitted to work Off-Site, such as at-home)'. Please be sure to price this discount in your overall price proposal when submitting bids against off-site RFQs.

Period of Performance: 2027 BASE: 1 January 2027 – 30 June 2027, with the possibility to exercise deliverables from the following options: 2027 Option: 1 July 2027 – 20 December 2027; 2028 Option: 1 January 2028 – 30 June 2028.

Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET

Special Terms and Conditions: Please consult the Statement of Work below.

Note: Please see separately dissemianted schedule of deliverables

STATEMENT OF WORK

Intelligence Systems E-Learning / Micro Lesson / Wiki Development SME Support — NCIA, The Hague, JISRC

1. INTRODUCTION

This SOW is related to delivery of support services within the NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA), an organization of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).

To strengthen the Alliance through connecting its forces, the NCIA delivers secure, coherent, cost effective and interoperable communications and information systems in support of consultation, command & control and enabling intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities for NATO, where and when required. It includes IT support to the Alliance's business processes (to include provision of IT shared services) to the NATO HQ, the Command Structure and NATO Agencies.

The Agency is an innovative and trusted Alliance partner and achieves its short- and long-term goals and objectives through the application of strategy-focused organizational principles, to which these support services are directly linked.

NCIA operations are underscored by the organization's core values and vision to be an essential, one-team contributor to NATO success.

2. NCIA BUSINESS AREA

The work shall commence under the auspices of the JISR Centre and shall continue under the equivalent JISR function or organizational entity following completion of the ongoing reorganization, without interruption to scope, deliverables, or contractual obligations.

3. NCIA JISR TEAM

The work will be conducted within a team of NCIA JISR training experts, a graphics designer and members from SHAPE J2.

4. OBJECTIVE AND TIMELINE

The objective of this request is to design, develop, and deliver a series of interactive micro lessons focused on key functionalities of an intelligence application, including Product Dissemination, Battlespace Objects (BSO), Request for Information (RFI), and ISR Collection Management (CM). The training will support onboarding, skill sustainment, and operational effectiveness for end users.

5. SCOPE OF WORK

The contractor shall:

  • Develop a storyboard, script and instructional design plan for each functional area.
  • Produce interactive micro lessons (3–7 minutes each) that include multimedia, voiceover, and assessment.
  • Ensure all training content adheres to classification, security, and accessibility standards.
  • Deliver in close cooperation with the graphic designer, SCORM-compliant training modules suitable for use in a secure Learning Management System (LMS).
  • Embed the micro lessons in WIKI pages that are online available in the NATO Software Factory (NSF) repository. If no WIKI page exists for the micro lesson, a new page must be created.

6. FUNCTIONAL AREAS AND DELIVERABLES

The following functional areas make up the scope of the micro lessons, with an initial estimated distribution of lessons per area:

Product Repository: Micro Lessons Baseline: 4. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 4. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 4. Description: Uploading, tagging, metadata, and search.

BSO Area: Micro Lessons Baseline: 5. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 5. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 5. Description: Defining BSOs, deriving from documents, linking to other modules, OPFOR Analysis.

RFI Workflow: Micro Lessons Baseline: 4. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 4. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 4. Description: Submitting RFIs, tracking lifecycle, intelligence gaps, MOE/MOP analysis.

CM Management: Micro Lessons Baseline: 5. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 5. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 5. Description: Managing ISR Organizations, managing Own CRs, submitting CRs for action, managing CTLs and Priority Schemes.

Collection Operations Management: Micro Lessons Baseline: 4. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 4. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 4. Description: Managing Collection and Exploitation Assets. Tasking assets with Collection Requests.

OPFOR Ballistic Missile Analysis: Micro Lessons Baseline: 4. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 4. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 4. Description: Reporting on Historical Firing Event (HFE), OPFOR BM Courses Of Action development and monitoring.

Warning Problem Management: Micro Lessons Baseline: 4. Micro Lessons 2027 Option: 4. Micro Lessons 2028 Option: 4. Description: Defining Warning Problems with sets of Indicators and sub-indicators. Reporting on indicators. MOP analysis.

Note: The distribution over the categories is an initial estimate that will be adjusted during the contract period.

7. DELIVERABLES AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE

A total of 30 finalized SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 compliant micro lessons (see note in Section 6).

Source files (editable format such as Articulate, Adobe Captivate, or Camtasia).

Job aids (optional, 1–2 pages per area).

Completion of up to two review cycles per module with client feedback.

The work is divided over 30 deliverables with options for 30 additional deliverables in the period 1 July 2027 – 20 December 2027 and 30 deliverables in the period 1 January 2028 – 30 June 2028.

7.1 Deliverable Planning

Objective: Clearly articulate what users should be able to do after each micro lesson and break these into modules aligned with the application areas.

Kick-off meeting: On the first day of the first deliverable, a kick-off meeting with the contractor, the SHAPE sponsor and the NCIA POC will be held at the NCIA facility in The Hague, NLD to plan the objectives of upcoming deliverables to meet the agreed deliverables.

7.2 Deliverable-Specific KPIs and Acceptance Criteria

7.2.1 Training Analysis and Instructional-Design Baseline

Functional coverage: Target 100%. The plan covers Product Dissemination, BSO, RFI, ISR CM, BM and I&W and maps each required function to at least one learning objective.

Learning-objective quality: Target 100%. Every lesson has measurable, action-oriented objectives describing what the learner must be able to perform in the application.

Requirements traceability: Target 100%. A traceability matrix links requirements, application functions, objectives, lesson content, interactions and assessment questions.

Micro-learning compliance: Target 100%. Lessons are designed for a target duration of 3–7 minutes, excluding optional reference material.

Design consistency: Target 100%. Approved templates define visual style, terminology, narration, interactions, feedback, assessments and WIKI presentation.

Schedule completeness: Target 100%. The production schedule identifies reviews, dependencies, subject-matter expert inputs, graphic-design activities and acceptance dates.

Acceptance requires approval by the SHAPE sponsor and the NCIA POC representing the product owner and functional subject-matter experts.

7.2.2 Storyboards, Scripts and Instructional-Design Plans

Storyboard completion: Target 100%. An approved storyboard exists for every contracted micro lesson.

Functional accuracy: Target ≥95% first-review approval. Procedures, screen flows, terminology and expected results are validated by the relevant subject-matter expert.

Script completeness: Target 100%. Narration, on-screen text, visual directions, interactions and assessment feedback are included.

Classification compliance: Target zero violations. Scripts and proposed media contain no information above the authorized classification or releasability level.

Review-cycle efficiency: Target maximum two consolidated correction cycles. Excludes revisions resulting from Purchaser-requested scope or application changes after baseline approval.

Acceptance requires consolidated approval of the storyboard and script before production starts. Production undertaken before approval remains at the Contractor's risk.

7.2.3 Functional Micro Lessons

The following KPIs apply separately to each functional area.

Required functional coverage: Target 100%. All approved learning objectives and functional steps are demonstrated or practiced.

Lesson duration: Target 3–7 minutes. Runtime is within range unless the Purchaser approves a justified exception in writing.

Functional accuracy: Target 100% for critical steps; ≥98% overall. No incorrect system behaviour, procedural step, role, status, field or expected result.

Interaction completion: Target 100%. All buttons, navigation controls, hotspots, branches, simulations and feedback mechanisms operate correctly.

Voiceover quality: Target 100% intelligible. Narration is clear, correctly pronounced, synchronized and free from disruptive noise or clipping.

SCORM compliance: Target 100%. Package passes the agreed SCORM conformance test.

Browser/display compatibility: Target 100% of approved test matrix. Module operates in all Purchaser-approved browser, resolution and workstation configurations.

Critical/high defects at acceptance: Target zero. No open Severity 1 or Severity 2 defects.

Medium defects at acceptance: Target zero, unless waived. Any exception requires a documented workaround and written Purchaser approval.

Schedule performance: Target ≥90% on time. Lessons are submitted by their approved milestone dates.

A functional-area deliverable is accepted when:

1. Its storyboard and script were previously approved.

2. All required lesson files and source files are delivered.

3. The module passes functional, content, accessibility, security and SCORM testing.

4. The relevant subject-matter expert validates functional accuracy.

5. No critical or high-severity defects remain open.

6. The Purchaser signs the applicable acceptance record.

7.2.4 Security, Accessibility and Technical Compliance

Classification markings: Target 100%. Modules, media, WIKI pages, metadata, files and supporting documents carry the correct classification and handling markings.

Security violations: Target zero. No unauthorized disclosure, external dependency, prohibited content, credential, operational data or unapproved network connection is present.

Authorized asset use: Target 100%. Images, recordings, fonts, icons, audio and application captures are approved and have documented usage rights or ownership.

Text alternatives: Target 100%. Meaningful visual and audio content has an appropriate caption, label, transcript or alternative description.

Colour and readability: Target 100%. Colour, contrast and text readability meet the applicable standard.

SCORM validation: Target 100%. Each package passes an agreed validation tool and target-LMS test.

External calls/dependencies: Target zero unless approved. Packages do not access the public internet, external analytics, cloud fonts, external libraries or unauthorized services.

Malware scan: Target 100% clean. All delivered packages and source files pass the Purchaser-approved malware-scanning process.

Compliance evidence: Target 100%. A checklist and test report are delivered for each module.

Classification and security are mandatory acceptance gates. A lesson that fails either gate is rejected regardless of its score against other KPIs.

7.2.5 NSF Repository and WIKI Integration

WIKI page coverage: Target 100%. Every micro lesson is embedded in an existing suitable WIKI page or has a newly created page.

Availability: Target 100% at acceptance. Purchaser can access the lesson from its WIKI page in the NSF environment.

Navigation and links: Target 100% functional. All lesson, breadcrumb, related-content and return-navigation links operate correctly.

Metadata completeness: Target 100%. Each page contains the agreed title, functional area, description, audience, duration, version, owner, date and classification marking.

Repository completeness: Target 100%. Approved source files, build files, release packages, documentation and configuration items are stored in the correct repository locations.

Version traceability: Target 100%. The deployed WIKI content and SCORM package can be traced to an approved repository version or release tag.

Secure rendering: Target zero security exceptions. Embedded content does not bypass access control or introduce unauthorized scripts, plug-ins or external calls.

Acceptance requires a successful end-to-end demonstration from the NSF WIKI page through lesson launch and completion, using an authorized user account in the designated environment.

7.2.6 Final Acceptance and Handover

Deliverable completeness: Target 100%. All approved lessons, SCORM packages, WIKI pages, source files and documentation are included.

Requirements traceability closure: Target 100%. Every requirement is shown as accepted, waived or formally deferred by the Purchaser.

Open critical/high defects: Target zero. No Severity 1 or Severity 2 defects remain.

Final acceptance: Target signed approval. The Purchaser issues a final acceptance certificate or equivalent written approval.

7.3 Generic Performance KPIs

These KPIs apply across all deliverables.

Milestone delivery: Target ≥90% on time. Measurement: Deliverables submitted by the contractual dates ÷ deliverables due.

First-pass acceptance: Target ≥85%. Measurement: Deliverables accepted without material rework ÷ deliverables submitted.

Review response time: Target ≤5 working days. Measurement: Time from receipt of consolidated comments to submission of corrections.

Requirements coverage: Target 100%. Measurement: Accepted requirements implemented ÷ applicable requirements.

Critical/high defect leakage: Target zero. Measurement: Severity 1–2 defects discovered after acceptance.

Defect correction: Target Critical and High: 3 days; Medium: 5 days. Measurement: Time between confirmed defect notification and corrected delivery.

Configuration traceability: Target 100%. Measurement: Deliverables with identifiable version, status, source and approval record.

Status reporting: Target 100% on time. Measurement: Reports delivered by agreed reporting date.

Risk escalation: Target within 1 working day. Measurement: Material risks notified after identification.

Stakeholder satisfaction: Target ≥4/5. Measurement: Purchaser rating covering quality, cooperation, responsiveness and usability.

Schedule KPIs should exclude delays caused solely by unavailable Purchaser environments, late consolidated feedback, late access approvals or approved scope changes, provided the Contractor records and reports the dependency promptly.

7.4 Acceptance Process

Each deliverable should follow this process:

1. Contractor quality review: The Contractor completes internal content, technical, security, accessibility and configuration checks.

2. Formal submission: The deliverable is submitted with a delivery note, version identifier, requirements traceability, test evidence and known-defect statement.

3. Purchaser review: The Purchaser has, for example, 10 working days to accept or provide one consolidated set of comments.

4. Correction: The Contractor addresses valid non-conformities within five working days, unless another period is agreed based on complexity.

5. Retest: Corrected elements and affected regression areas are retested.

6. Decision: The Purchaser accepts, conditionally accepts or rejects the deliverable in writing.

7. Payment authorization: Payment is released only for an accepted or formally conditionally accepted milestone.

Silence or use of a draft deliverable should not constitute acceptance. Defect severity is defined as follows:

Severity 1 – Critical: Definition: Security/classification breach, module cannot launch, data or LMS integrity risk, or lesson is unusable. Acceptance effect: Automatic rejection.

Severity 2 – High: Definition: Required functionality, assessment, accessibility function or LMS tracking fails with no viable workaround. Acceptance effect: Rejection until corrected.

Severity 3 – Medium: Definition: Material content, synchronization, navigation or presentation defect with a workaround. Acceptance effect: Correct before acceptance unless expressly waived.

Severity 4 – Low: Definition: Minor cosmetic or editorial issue that does not impede learning. Acceptance effect: May be recorded for correction in an agreed maintenance release.

7.5 Deliverable and Payment Schedule

Payment milestone cycles are at the last working day of the calendar month in which the deliverables occurred. Upon completion and validation of each deliverable and at the end of the monthly milestone, all completed deliverables for that month can be submitted for payment.

If, due to unavailability of the contractor, a deliverable is not delivered or is delivered incomplete by the end of the deliverable period, it will be considered void and no payment will occur.

The payment shall be dependent upon successful acceptance as specified in the KPIs. This will follow the payment milestones and shall include a completed Delivery Acceptance Sheet (DAS), signed by the Contractor and project authority, and an invoice from the contractor.

Payments should be milestone-based and made only after formal acceptance of the corresponding deliverable. Interim delivery, upload or demonstration does not constitute acceptance.

If the contractor fails to meet the agreed acceptance criteria for any task, NCIA reserves the right to withhold payment for that task/deliverable.

NCIA JISRC: Project lead and main stakeholder.

SHAPE J2/6: Sponsor and subject-matter expert (SME).

Contractor: To provide services and deliverables as identified above.

2027 BASE: 1 January 2027 – 30 June 2027

Deliverable 01: 30 deliverables. Payment Milestones: End of the calendar month for all deliverables completed and accepted within the respective month.

2027 Options: 1 July 2027 – 20 December 2027

Deliverable 02: 30 deliverables. Cost Ceiling: Price per deliverable will be determined by applying the price adjustment formula as outlined in CO-115786-AAS+ Special Provisions article 6.5. Payment Milestones: End of the calendar month for all deliverables completed and accepted within the respective month.

2028 Option: 1 January 2028 – 30 June 2028

Deliverable 03: 30 deliverables. Cost Ceiling: Price per deliverable will be determined by applying the price adjustment formula as outlined in CO-115786-AAS+ Special Provisions article 6.5. Payment Milestones: End of the calendar month for all deliverables completed and accepted within the respective month.

8. SCHEDULE

The BASE period of performance is as soon as possible but not later than 1 January 2027 and will end no later than 30 June 2027. If the 2027 option is exercised, the periods of performance are 1 July 2027 – 20 December 2027. If the 2028 option is exercised, the period of performance are 1 January 2028 – 30 June 2028.

9. CONSTRAINTS

All the documentation provided under this statement of work will be based on NCIA templates or agreed with the project POC. All support, maintenance and documentation will be stored under configuration management and/or in the provided NCIA tools and systems.

All developed solutions under this project will be property of NCIA.

10. SECURITY

The performance of these services requires a valid NATO SECRET security clearance prior to the start of the engagement. The expected classification level of the deliverables is NATO UNCLASSIFIED.

The execution of the services may require the contractors to access information, as well as CIS systems, classified up to NATO SECRET. At NCIA or other NATO sites, the highest level of classification that contractors may need to access is NATO SECRET (NS).

11. TRAVEL

The contractor will provide the services under this SOW at their own premises but may need to travel to NATO sites in support of the project including NCIA in The Hague, NCI Academy in Oeiras as needed and NATO Command Structure Sites.

It is anticipated that, during the base period and each option, the work will require three two-day visits to NCIA The Hague (NLD), one three-day visit to the NCI Academy in Oeiras (PRT), and one three-day visit to HQ SHAPE in Mons (BEL).

12. QUALIFICATIONS

[See Requirements]

13. GENERAL PROVISIONS

NCIA Recognised Business Hours/Holidays: The NCIA-The Hague official holiday schedule applies and will be provided to the contractor. NCIA Hours of Operations: Monday to Thursday 0830–1700 and Friday 0830–1500 (CET).

jobs.title: Technical Sourcer/Researcher
jobs.excerpt: Most sourcing jobs hand you a title and a target number.
jobs.description:
Most sourcing jobs hand you a title and a target number. This one hands you a market and asks you to understand it better than anyone else has.

Our client is a boutique, retained executive search firm in the United States, founded and run by former in-house talent leaders from some of the best-known technology companies in the world. They deliberately keep a small caseload. Every search is retained, every search is researched from scratch, and their stated thesis is that hiring should be driven by data and original research rather than by whoever happens to be qualified and available. That thesis only works if someone is doing the research. That someone is you.

As their Technical Sourcer / Talent Researcher, you are the research engine behind every search. You will chart the talent ecosystem around a role before a single message goes out, map team structures and reporting lines at the companies that build the strongest people, track who is scaling and who is contracting, and surface senior engineers, product leaders, designers and analytics people that other firms never reach. Your research feeds directly into how each search is positioned, who gets targeted, and how the outreach is written.

You will work alongside the firm's recruiters and managing partners, joining kickoff calls and debriefs, and you will be expected to tell them the truth about a market early — including when the truth is that the brief will not clear it. This is a role for someone who finds genuine satisfaction in a complete, defensible map of a niche, and who would rather deliver eighty names that all belong than three hundred that mostly do not.

Key Responsibilities

Market Mapping & Talent Research

  • Lead deep-dive research to chart the full talent ecosystem around each search, turning a hard search into a solvable one
  • Map team structures, reporting lines and headcount at target startups and at the larger incumbents that feed them
  • Identify where the strongest Engineering, Product, Design and Analytics talent is concentrated across high-growth sectors such as AI/ML, fintech, SaaS, security and adjacent verticals — and develop a view on why it clusters there
  • Track talent movement, promotion patterns and organizational shifts at high-talent-density companies
  • Deliver market maps that give the recruiting team and their clients a clear, actionable picture of the landscape, including its limits

Talent Intelligence

  • Go beyond names: build a point of view on headcount trends, funding rounds, org changes and competitor hiring movement within each target sector
  • Research which companies are scaling, which are contracting, and where strong people are likely to become available in the next two quarters
  • Translate that intelligence into research outputs that shape positioning and search strategy, not just lists of names and contact details
  • Surface market constraints and competitive dynamics while there is still time to change the plan

Strategic Sourcing

  • Build high-signal candidate pipelines for senior individual contributor and leadership roles, spanning Staff through Principal and Director through VP
  • Use LinkedIn Recruiter at a power-user level: layered Boolean, precise filters, projects, spotlights and the platform features that surface people a standard keyword search never returns
  • Source beyond LinkedIn using whatever channel the niche demands, including GitHub, Crunchbase, patent databases, academic publications, conference speaker lists and open-source contribution history
  • Curate rather than pad — every name on a list belongs there, and you can say exactly why

Search Strategy & Calibration

  • Partner on calibration and search design so that research directly informs positioning, target company lists and outreach strategy from day one
  • Join search kickoff calls and debriefs so sourcing stays aligned as the brief evolves
  • Recommend concrete adjustments when the research shows the original brief will not clear the market — a wider stage band, an adjacent domain, a relaxed must-have, a different geography

Data Integrity & Documentation

  • Maintain accurate, well-organized and immediately actionable Google Sheets across every active market map and candidate list
  • Keep formatting consistent, data current, and documentation clear enough that anyone on the recruiting team can open a sheet and act on it without cleanup or clarification
  • Maintain source tracking, search methodology notes and candidate status documentation for every active search
  • Treat data hygiene as a professional standard rather than an afterthought

Collaboration & Communication

  • Work closely with recruiters and managing partners to translate client briefs into targeted research strategies
  • Communicate findings proactively and in real time, including the uncomfortable ones: thin talent availability, market constraints, pipeline gaps
  • Flag candidate quality issues and research dead ends early enough for the strategy to change rather than late enough to explain a miss

Requirements

    • Substantial hands-on experience in sourcing or talent research for engineering or technology roles. We are looking for roughly four years or more, and the depth of the work matters more to us than the exact number.
    • LinkedIn Recruiter mastery. You have worked from a paid Recruiter seat as a daily tool, not an occasional one, and you can build the search that finds the needle rather than the haystack.
    • Experience sourcing for United States based technology companies, ideally venture-backed startups from seed through Series D.
    • Research depth. You are comfortable spending hours inside a single niche to produce a complete, defensible map of the market and the hundred best people in it.
    • Startup fluency. You understand talent density across the ecosystem, which organizations build the strongest people, and what it takes to thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.
    • Investigative instinct. You do not stop at the obvious sources. You triangulate across GitHub, patents, publications, conference talks and company team pages to reach people who are not findable any other way.
    • Strong data organization in Google Sheets. Your sheets are clean, logical and useful to anyone who opens them.
    • Clear, confident written English. You can explain a market to someone who has not looked at it, in writing, without being asked twice.
  • Preferred Qualifications
    • Background at a boutique, retained or executive search firm that runs a research-driven methodology
    • Experience building market maps or talent ecosystem analyses for specific sectors such as AI/ML, fintech, SaaS, security, defense technology or climate
    • Hands-on sourcing through GitHub, Crunchbase, patent databases or other non-LinkedIn research methods
    • Familiarity with funding stages and venture ecosystem dynamics — you know what separates a Series A from a Series D, and what that difference means for talent
    • Experience delivering candidate intelligence reports or market briefings to recruiting leadership or to clients directly
    • Exposure to searches at the Staff, Principal, Director or VP level rather than only at junior and mid levels
  • Tools & Platforms
    • LinkedIn Recruiter — primary sourcing platform; advanced proficiency required
    • GitHub — engineering talent sourcing and contribution analysis
    • Crunchbase — company research, funding tracking and headcount intelligence
    • Google Sheets — market map and candidate list management
    • Patent and publication databases — sourcing for specialized technical talent
    • An ATS or CRM as assigned — candidate tracking and pipeline management
    • Microsoft Teams for day-to-day collaboration, and Hubstaff for time tracking
  • What Makes You a Great Fit
    • You treat every search like an investigation. You do not stop when the obvious candidates are found; you keep digging.
    • Your lists are curated, not padded. Every name belongs, and you can defend why it is there.
    • You are genuinely curious about markets, companies and talent ecosystems. You read funding announcements and engineering blogs for your own interest, not because someone told you to.
    • Your data is always clean. The recruiting team can open your market map and act on it immediately, without asking you a single clarifying question.
    • You say what you are finding in real time. If a market is tighter than expected or a sector is talent-constrained, you raise it early and bring options with you.
    • You would rather be measured on precision than on volume, and you are comfortable defending a shorter list.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Up to $8/hour
  • 100% remote work
  • Full-time role

We hire for the long haul, so a steady track record of staying and growing always moves you up our list.

To apply:

Ensure your LinkedIn profile and resume are up-to-date and comprehensive (submit a comprehensive resume in English, PDF format), and complete the assessment in this link:

A quick note on how we will reach you: our recruitment team communicates primarily through Telegram, using the mobile number on your application and resume. Please make sure that number is active and registered on Telegram, since this is where screening and interview scheduling happen. If it is not registered yet, you can set it up right after you apply — it takes only a few minutes and keeps your application moving without delay.

By applying, you consent to being contacted via the contact information provided in your application for recruitment purposes only.

Because of the volume of applications we receive, we're only able to follow up directly with candidates whose experience closely matches this role. If you don't hear from us within 10 days, please know we genuinely appreciate your interest—and we'd welcome your application to future openings that may be a stronger fit. Thank you for considering Remote Raven, and all the best in your search.

A note on scheduling: initial interviews run in US Mountain Standard Time (MST) within a 3:00 AM – 1:00 PM MST window. We know that takes flexibility around the time difference, and we genuinely appreciate it.

Instacart's Strategic Finance team partners across the business to drive disciplined growth and long-term value creation. Within this group, Consolidation is responsible for being the aggregated source of truth for how Instacart performs and where it's headed. As Director, Strategic Finance – Consolidation, you will own this responsibility and sit at the center of our financial ecosystem — integrating inputs from Accounting, other parts of StratFin, Business Operations teams, Investor Relations, and more — into one coherent, reconciled, and forward-looking view of the company.

This is a high-visibility role at the heart of Instacart's financial governance. Reporting to the Vice President of Investor Relations and Strategic Finance, you will be the architect of our consolidated P&L forecast, our long-range financial model, and the financial narratives that inform our Board, investors, and executive team. As Instacart continues to mature as a public company, this function is foundational to how we govern the business and tell our financial story.

The ideal candidate is a rigorous financial operator and natural integrator — someone who sees the forest, not just the trees. You know how to land the quarter while simultaneously anticipating what's around short-, medium-, and long-term corners. You consolidate narratives and key business insights across teams into a single, coherent point of view. You earn the trust of senior stakeholders through consistently high-quality work, lead a high-performing team, and set the bar for what great looks like.

What you'll cook up in your first year

Own the consolidated financial view

  • A single, reconciled consolidated P&L forecast is in place and trusted — integrating inputs from the broader StratFin team, Accounting, Business Operations, Investor Relations and more.
  • The monthly and quarterly close cycle runs on time and at executive-quality standards, with variance analysis and management reporting packages that connect results to business drivers — not just numbers on a page.
  • A GAAP and non-GAAP long-range financial model (5-year) reflects current strategy and updated assumptions, with scenario analysis that helps leadership anticipate what's around the corner.
  • The annual budgeting process is orchestrated end-to-end, with company-level targets set clearly and cross-functional alignment secured.

Be the financial narrator for Instacart's story

  • Board decks, investor materials, and quarterly business review packages are delivered consistently — accurate, insightful, and requiring minimal revision from senior leadership.
  • Our weekly consolidated P&L outlook is a trusted executive staple, surfacing not just what happened, but what it means and what's coming.
  • Cross-team narratives and business insights are synthesized into a single, coherent point of view — so leadership always knows where the business stands and what decisions need to be made.

Build the infrastructure that makes it all scalable

  • Forecasting processes that are repeatable, auditable, and aligned with Accounting's close process.
  • Business Unit P&Ls are designed and live, enabling clearer accountability and more rigorous investment decisions.
  • Internal capital allocation decisions are timely, organized and effective — providing financial frameworks to seamlessly align and execute key business decisions.

Grow the team and raise the bar

  • A high-performing team is operating at a consistently elevated standard — stronger analytical rigor, sharper business judgment, and clear ownership across the function.
  • Cross-functional partners — including the CFO, Strategic Finance, Accounting, Investor Relations, Legal, and other Business partners — rely on this function as a proactive, trusted advisor, not just a reporting engine.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

  • 12+ years of experience in a relevant field with demonstrated financial acumen and a track record of leveraging data to drive business impact
  • Proven experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, or Strategic Finance at a high-growth or public technology company, with direct ownership of consolidated financial reporting and forecasting processes
  • Deep understanding of GAAP financial statements and comfort operating across both GAAP and non-GAAP financial frameworks
  • High proficiency in advanced Excel/Sheets with a demonstrated ability to build and maintain complex, enterprise-grade financial models
  • Trusted partner to cross-functional leadership, including Accounting, IR, and Business Ops; effectively influences stakeholders to secure alignment on complex strategic recommendations
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills—able to distill complex financial data into crisp, actionable narratives for the Board, C-suite, and business partners
  • Strong people management experience with a track record of developing high-performing Finance teams and raising the bar on analytical quality and process discipline
  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities, and deliver in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

  • MBA preferred
  • Experience building or significantly transforming a consolidation or Corporate/Strategic Finance function, particularly in the context of a high-paced, newly public company.
  • Familiarity with financial planning systems such as Adaptive, Oracle, Workiva, Pigment, Anaplan, or similar enterprise FP&A tools
  • Intermediate to advanced SQL proficiency—comfortable leveraging datasets to pressure-test assumptions, improve reporting, and uncover actionable insights
  • Experience with consumer marketplace businesses or on-demand commerce
  • Demonstrated enthusiasm for applying AI and automation tools to financial forecasting, reporting, and analytical workflows
  • Ability to work from our San Francisco or New York City office on occasion
