jobs.title: MBA Intern, Strategy & Development
jobs.excerpt: Soluna is on a mission to solve one of renewable energy’s biggest challenges: wasted power.
jobs.description:
Soluna is on a mission to solve one of renewable energy’s biggest challenges: wasted power. Our data centersconvert excesssolar, hydro, and windenergy into productive computational work, such as Bitcoin mining, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. By co-locating with renewable power sources, we bring demand directly to the source,helping power plants increase revenue while contributing more megawatts to the grid.

We are looking for an MBA Intern, Development & Strategy to join our world-class team.

The Opportunity

Soluna's growth depends on finding the right sites before anyone else does. Every week, inbound leads arrive from independent power producers, renewable developers, landowners, and brokers — and our team sources many more. Most of them will not work. A small number are exceptional. The difference between the two is a disciplined screen: is there curtailed or low-cost power, is there a credible path to interconnection, is there land, fiber, and water, and does the arithmetic clear our return threshold?

This internship owns the front end of that funnel. You will take raw leads, run them through Soluna's qualification criteria, build a first-pass economic screen, and produce a clear recommendation on whether the opportunity advances to full diligence or gets a fast, well-reasoned no. The modeling is deliberately light — enough to size the opportunity and pressure-test the assumptions, not a full project finance build. Speed and judgment matter more than precision at this stage.

This is a high-ownership role on a small team: your screens will be read by the people who decide where Soluna builds next.

What You'll Do

Lead Qualification & Screening

  • Run inbound and sourced leads through Soluna's qualification framework — power cost and curtailment profile, interconnection status and queue position, land control, fiber and water availability, and counterparty credibility.
  • Produce a standard one-page qualification summary for each lead so the team can make a go / no-go call quickly and consistently.
  • Recommend advance, park, or pass on every opportunity you touch, with the reasoning written down — including the reasoning behind the passes.
  • Maintain the lead intake queue so nothing sits unreviewed and the team always knows what is waiting.

Light Financial Modeling

  • Build first-pass economic screens for qualified sites — estimated cost of power, capacity sizing, indicative capex, and top-line return.
  • Run sensitivities on the variables that actually move the answer, such as energy price, curtailment hours, hashprice or contracted AI/HPC revenue, and time to energization.
  • Pressure-test counterparty assumptions against market data and flag where a lead's claims are not supported by the underlying economics.
  • Keep the screening model clean and reusable so the team can run it without you after the internship ends.

Market & Pipeline Intelligence

  • Track opportunities across ERCOT, SPP, MISO, and PJM, including interconnection queue movement and curtailment trends that create new leads.
  • Update the pipeline tracker and executive summary so leadership has a current view of what is in the funnel and where it stands.
  • Research specific markets, utilities, or counterparties on demand to support live deal conversations.
  • Present a summer project to the Development & Strategy team and senior leadership — a durable improvement to how Soluna screens and qualifies opportunities.

What You Bring

Required

  • Currently enrolled in an MBA program, with an expected graduation date following the internship period.
  • Strong Excel modeling skills — comfortable building a screening model from a blank sheet, not just editing someone else's.
  • Demonstrated analytical judgment: the ability to reach a defensible answer with incomplete information and say clearly what you do not know.
  • Clear, concise written communication; you can compress a complicated opportunity into one page a busy executive will actually read.
  • Genuine interest in energy, digital infrastructure, or the intersection of the two.

Preferred

  • Prior experience in energy, infrastructure, project finance, investment banking, private equity, or corporate development.
  • Familiarity with U.S. wholesale power markets, interconnection processes, or renewable project development.
  • Exposure to market data platforms such as Orennia, Velocity Suite, or similar.
  • Working knowledge of Bitcoin mining economics or AI/HPC data center demand drivers.
  • Comfort building in PowerPoint for investor- and board-facing audiences.

Why join Soluna?

We are a diverse, driven team of entrepreneurs, energy experts, private equity leaders, storytellers and engineers. We are passionate about making the world greener and we have conviction about how we will bring change on a global scale.

We are equally as zealous about championing our teams, relentless about developing our people, and believe strongly that Soluna’s goals and commitment to our mission are strengthened by our employee’s voices.

jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Most companies are layering AI onto existing processes. This role is about something different: rebuilding those processes from the ground up, so teams can do work that actually matters.

Instacart's Marketing team has set ambitious AI goals — and this is the person who makes them real. You'll be the first role of this kind in Marketing, embedded in the org with a clear mandate: identify what's slow, manual, or broken across the Marketing organization and rebuild it into something fundamentally better. The benchmark isn't marginal improvement. It's transformation — building solutions that make people wonder how they ever worked without them.

This is a builder role. Strategy is a means to an end. The end is something shipped, adopted, and measurable. You'll also be the connective tissue for Marketing's AI ambitions — convening the people who own AI goals, unblocking what's stuck, and creating internal momentum that makes the whole org move faster.

What you'll cook up in your first year

Building (60%)

  • Identify high-impact workflows, systems, and processes across Marketing that are slow, manual, or duct-taped together — and rebuild them AI-natively, from the ground up
  • Own the full cycle: understand the current state, design the solution, build it, ship it — then measure what changed. Establish the before, prove the after, and make the case to leadership
  • Walk in with work already queued. Early builds include:
    • Recurring leadership and planning narratives — transforming how Marketing produces its MBR, quarterly planning summaries, budget variance write-ups, and channel performance narratives; currently manual synthesis across multiple inputs, rebuilt into a faster, more consistent, AI-native output
    • Integrated campaign launch process — automating key steps from campaign ideation to launch, reducing the manual handoffs and coordination overhead that slow campaigns down across teams
    • Brief quality and standardization — an AI review layer that evaluates briefs before they leave the building, flags what's missing or unclear, and raises input quality across the org before downstream teams absorb the cost of a bad brief
  • Build with portability in mind — your solutions should be constructed so others can pick them up, adapt them for their own context, and extend what you've built without starting from scratch; you're not just solving a problem, you're creating infrastructure others can build on
  • Develop and maintain an intake framework: gather inputs from across the org, evaluate feasibility and impact, and make a defensible call on what gets built next — including what doesn't; prioritization discipline means saying no to low-value requests as readily as yes to high-value ones

Driving Adoption (20%)

  • Own the change management side of every build: create the conditions for people to trust what you've built, use it consistently, and not revert to old habits when something feels unfamiliar
  • Evangelize internally — write up wins, build case studies, show other teams what's possible; your goal is to generate more demand than you can supply, which means the org needs to see what AI can actually do, not just hear about it
  • Create energy around AI across Marketing — not as a cheerleader, but as someone who shows people things they didn't know were possible and makes it easy for them to take the next step

Orchestration & Thought Partnership (20%)

  • Lead the MarComms AI KR forum: convene AI KR owners across Marketing, create momentum behind shared goals, surface blockers, and hold the operating cadence
  • Act as a working partner to AI goal owners — unblocking vendor delays, solving capability gaps, helping people get unstuck

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

  • 7+ years in marketing operations, marketing strategy, or a closely adjacent discipline — you understand how marketing orgs work, where the friction lives, and what it costs to leave it unfixed
  • Proven builder with a track record of impact — you have shipped AI-powered workflows and processes that demonstrably changed how teams work; you can name the problem, describe the solution, and quantify the result. You’re so invested in AI that you’ve applied it beyond the scope of your current role.
  • Hands-on daily experience with frontier AI tools such as Claude, GPT-4o, or Gemini, including writing prompts that produce reliable, production-quality output at scale
  • Experience building agentic systems where AI components interact with each other, including multi-agent design, orchestration layers, and workflows that run without a human in the loop at every step
  • An adoption-minded approach to building: designing for adoption from day one and taking accountability for whether what you built actually gets used
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain what you're building, why it matters, and where it stands, for audiences from ICs to CMO-level leadership
  • Prioritization discipline — you can evaluate a request and tell someone their problem isn't a good AI candidate right now, or that the cost of building outstrips the benefit; you know what not to build

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

  • A framework for evaluating AI vendors and tools quickly, including running comparison pilots and making principled decisions about what earns a place in the stack

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are About StripeStripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses.
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

Metronome is the leading usage-based billing platform built for modern software companies. With Metronome, companies can launch products faster, offer any pricing model, and streamline finance workflows without writing code. Our platform computes millions of invoices per billing period and is scaling rapidly to accommodate new customers, saving them hours of development time and manual invoicing and enabling them to use consumption data to better serve their customers. Our customers love our product and approach, and we’re humbled to work with amazing companies like OpenAI, Databricks, NVIDIA, Confluent, and Anthropic.

You'll be joining an experienced team that includes founders who have successfully built and sold startups before. Our founders and employees have direct experience building and scaling teams through massive growth at companies like Dropbox, Clever, and New Relic. On the back of this experience and our success-to-date, we’ve raised over $128M from leading investors including NEA, Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, Elad Gil, and Workday Ventures. We’re also proud to have founders and executives of companies like Segment, Plaid, Looker, Gitlab, Confluent, HashiCorp, and Snowflake, as investors who have experienced the pain we're solving firsthand.

About the team

The Solutions Architecture team at Metronome is a technical group that sits at the intersection of sales, growth, product, and R&D. In simple terms, we own the technical aspects of the customer lifecycle between after sales and before handoff to post-implementation teams.

As a member of the Solutions Architecture team, you’ll primarily be focused on ensuring customers successfully implement Metronome’s products and realize value quickly.

Responsibilities

  • Using proficient discovery and scoping to understand what challenges our clients face in billing, launching new products, pricing & packaging, quote-to-cash, customer experience, and related areas.
  • Doing whatever it takes to support clients throughout the entire implementation lifecycle, including requirements gathering, technical design, integration design, testing, data migration, and launch.
  • Providing expert guidance to clients regarding usage-based pricing and consumption business models.
  • Hands on configuration of Metronome’s system on behalf of clients
  • Designing integrations between Metronome’s APIs and the clients business systems to align to Metronome best practices (including CRM/ CPQ, Payments, Taxation, ERP, Billing Providers, Reporting and Analytics tools).
  • Acting as a liaison between the field and Metronome R&D to advocate for client needs and feature requests.
  • Partnering with implementation managers and other project team members to provide visibility into progress and proactively identify risks and issues
  • Building relationships with people at our client organizations, from day-to-day operators to C-Suite executives. We believe in meeting our customers in-person whenever possible.
  • Designing integrations of Metronome into prospect systems and consultatively influencing the direction of our prospects’ pricing and packaging.
  • Ensuring a proper handoff to our post-implementation teams (Customer Success and Technical Support).

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Expect these engagements to be complex, deep, technical, and most of all interesting. Metronome directly influences how the internet monetizes - AI is an obvious current example - and our group is on the front lines driving this influence with our prospects. Metronome is a startup. As such, there’s a lot still to figure out and tremendous room for high-agency people to impact our direction and strategy, build processes from zero to one, and generally make a difference. If this excites you as much as it excites us, let’s talk.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience working in technical and/or customer-facing roles involving SaaS products (for example, roles like sales engineering, solutions architecture, technical account management).
  • Deep knowledge of the quote-to-cash space, including integrating with or otherwise interacting with tools like Salesforce, NetSuite, CPQs, Billing, Tax, Payments, etc.
  • Experience leading complex, multi-phase technology transformation programs for enterprise companies.
  • Experience in fast-moving startup environments that value high agency.
  • Ability to quickly learn and communicate technical concepts to technical, go-to-market, and finance stakeholders.
  • Excitement for building and improving GTM playbooks, processes, and reusable assets.
  • Ability to travel approximately 30% of the time (will vary depending on client needs)

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience as a software engineer, product manager, or in other technical roles.
  • Strong understanding of project management and program management fundamentals and principles
  • Experience working with users from one or more of the following personas: Finance/ CFO, Engineering/ CTO, Product/ CPO, Sales Ops/ CRO, and Billing Operations.
  • Experience with logs, metrics, billing, finance, or other infrastructure or financial tooling and concepts.

jobs.description:
Type: Full-time (remote)

Reports to: Director of Marketplace (TikTok Lead)

Direct report: Creator Community Consultant

Compensation: $90,000 - $110,000 annually

About the role

Our TikTok creator community lives in Discord and is a core driver of TikTok Shop GMV. The Creator Coach + Creative Strategist handles the creative side — trends, angles, coaching. You own the business, management and strategy.

That means you own the structure, the economics, the growth, and the results of the community: how creators are recruited, how they're tiered, what products/offers they promote, what they're paid, what makes them stay, what contests do we run and what the whole program returns against what it costs. You're the operator who turns a Discord server full of creators into a predictable, scalable revenue channel- plus a creative engine to feed paid channels.

This is a strategy and operations role with a community wrapper around it — not a moderation job. If your instinct when you look at a creator program is to ask "what's the retention curve by cohort or what metric in the TikTok funnel is our constraint to unlock rapid growth," this is your role.

What you'll do

Own the program

  • Own the creator community end to end: structure, tiering, incentives, calendar, and outcomes.
  • Design and evolve the tier system — what qualifies a creator for each tier, what they get, and what's expected in return. Make the ladder something creators actually want to climb.
  • Build/manage/implement the incentive and commission architecture: commission rates, bonuses, contests, gifting and sample seeding, exclusivity where it makes sense. Model the economics before you launch anything.
  • Help build and manage the training program designed to take L1 creators to L3/L4.
  • Track cohorts of creators that enter and how they progress in terms of levels, GMV, etc.
  • Own the creator recruiting funnel: sourcing, application, vetting, onboarding. Keep a healthy top of funnel and a clear bar for who gets in.
  • Own creator retention. Churn is the quiet killer of every creator program — you'll know your cohort curves and be actively working against them; optimizing for videos per creator per period, etc.
  • Own weekly full-funnel reporting to identify where our constraints are: creators, volume, impressions, videos per creator, CVR%, GPM, etc.

Manage and enable

  • Manage the Creator Coach + Creative Strategist: set priorities, review output, hold the cadence, help them get better at the job.
  • Make sure the coaching program and the angle pipeline are actually producing — that creators are shipping, improving, and converting.
  • Run the operating rhythm: weekly community programming, monthly creator reviews, quarterly planning against channel targets

Report and coordinate

  • Own the numbers: active creators, videos shipped, view volume, breakout rate, conversion, GMV by creator and by tier, cost per video, program ROI. Report them weekly to the Director of Marketplace.
  • Translate community signal into strategy — what creators are saying about product, price, offers, and competitors is some of the best market research we have, and it should reach the right teams.
  • Work cross-functionally with paid media (best creator content becomes paid creative), brand, and ops/supply chain (sampling, seeding, inventory for creator demand).
  • Handle escalations: creator disputes, payment issues, content that's off-brand or non-compliant, and TikTok Shop policy questions.

Build the machine

  • Document the playbook. Everything from onboarding to tier promotion to contest mechanics should be repeatable.
  • Build the tooling and workflow: Discord structure, roles and permissions, bots and automations, tracking and attribution, payment ops.
  • Plan for scale. Design decisions should hold at 10x the creator count, not just today's roster.

How you work

  • High ownership. You're being handed a channel, not a task list.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and speed — this program will look different in six months and you'll be the one changing it.
  • Genuinely likes creators. The best community operators are the ones creators trust.

Requirements

  • 3–5+ years in creator/influencer/affiliate program management, community management, or growth marketing at a fast-growing consumer brand — with real ownership of a number, not just execution.
  • Experience running or scaling a Discord community.
  • Strong commercial instincts. You're comfortable in a spreadsheet, you can model incentive structures and unit economics, and you can defend a program's ROI.
  • Hands-on understanding of TikTok and TikTok Shop: how affiliate works, how commissions and attribution function, what actually drives GMV on the platform.
  • Excellent written communication. Most of your leadership happens in text, in public, in front of creators.
  • People management experience, or clear readiness for it.

Strong plus

  • Experience at a fast-growing TikTok shop consumer brand.
  • CPG or food & beverage background.
  • Familiarity with creator/affiliate tooling and Discord automation.
  • Some creator or content experience of your own — you don't have to be the creative brain, but credibility with creators helps.

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary designed to reward high performance and impact
  • 401(k) plan with company matching
  • Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Stock option plan so you can share in the value you help build
  • Generous paid time off and company holidays
  • Real ownership and autonomy to drive measurable growth
  • Ongoing professional development opportunities as we scale

QuantCo is offering up to ten AI Builder Grants to exceptional Bachelor’s and Master’s students enrolled at universities in Austria, Germany, and Switzerland. Grant recipients will receive a Max 5x subscription for Claude over five months, valued at over $500 per person to power their own AI projects, explore emerging tools, and gain exposure to state-of-the-art developments in artificial intelligence.

At QuantCo, our global teams of quants, AI and software engineers collaborate heavily with state-of-the-art AI tooling to build scalable, high-impact solutions for enterprise clients. We are introducing this grant to bridge the gap between academic environments and real-world coding best practices, helping eager students accelerate their technical skills outside the classroom. Whether you have previously competed in hackathons or are simply excited about building innovative projects, we encourage all ambitious students to apply and join us in shaping the AI transition.

To apply, please submit your CV and transcripts. We review applications on a rolling basis and will get back to you within a week of your submission. If you have any questions, please reach out to .

About QuantCo

At QuantCo, we leverage expertise in data science, engineering, and economics to help organizations turn data into decisions. Started by 4 PhDs from Harvard and Stanford, we are now more than 180 professionals with extensive quantitative, engineering, and business experience. We are globally distributed with offices in Berlin, Boston, Cologne, Karlsruhe, London, Munich, San Francisco, and Zurich.
Our solutions include algorithmic pricing, data-driven claims management, and high-dimensional forecasting systems. Our customers include some of the largest financial, retail, and healthcare organizations in the US and Europe. We impact core business processes and decisions by combining advanced data-driven insights with scalable engineering solutions.
We are excited about writing mission-critical code that affects millions of people and impacts billions of dollars. If you feel the same way, we look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Strategist
jobs.excerpt: DescriptionSprout Social is looking to hire a Product Marketing Strategist to the Marketing team who will help us stay ahead of our competitors and stand out with industry analysts.
jobs.description:
Description

Sprout Social is looking to hire a Product Marketing Strategist to the Marketing team who will help us stay ahead of our competitors and stand out with industry analysts.

Why join Sprout's Marketing team?

At Sprout Social, we don’t just market products—we set the pace for how breakthrough brands connect with the world. As the social intelligence platform powering the future of customer connection, our Marketing team is the driving force behind turning that vision into reality. We lead with clarity and act with speed to drive market leadership, generate demand, and accelerate customer expansion, all in close partnership with core cross-functional stakeholders.

Here, you’ll have the freedom to test bold ideas, learn fast, and shape the future of the global brands we empower. We measure success by the business results we create and a shared commitment to excellence in our craft. If you’re ready to own your impact, accelerate your career, and build the definitive system for business, this is where you belong.

What you’ll do

Competitive intelligence (about 70% of your time)

  • Track our key competitors. Conduct in-depth, always on analysis of our key competitors, spanning social media management, social listening, media monitoring and influencer marketing. Watch for product launches, pricing moves, marketing campaigns and company news.
  • Be our early warning system. Be the first person at Sprout Social to share updates on emerging platforms and new features from established providers.
  • Publish regular intelligence reports. Write clear, useful reports for stakeholders across research and development (R&D) and Product Marketing. Tell them what changed, why it matters and what we should do about it.
  • Respond fast when competitors move. When a competitor releases a new feature, run a quick analysis. Share the key points with Sales and Customer Success (CS) so they can answer customer questions with confidence.
  • Shape how we win. Go beyond reporting what competitors do. Recommend how we position against each one, where we can differentiate and what it will take to proactively win.
  • Jump into deals. Support Sales in live, competitive deals. Help set the deal strategy and arm reps with the right proof points.
  • Keep our competitive source of truth current. Maintain battlecards, comparison pages and talking points so customer-facing teams always have accurate information.
  • Build a network of sources. Gather intelligence from analyst reports, review sites, win-loss interviews, and conversations with Sales and CS teams.
  • Use AI to scale your work. Use AI tools to build core intelligence once, then systemize it across the company. Partner closely with our GTM Systems and Applied AI team in Revenue Operations to put competitive insight inside the tools Sales and CS use every day.

Analyst relations (about 30% of your time)

  • Manage our relationships with industry analysts. Coordinate briefings and inquiry calls with key analyst relations firms. Keep them up to date on Sprout Social's products, including NewsWhip, Listening, and Influencer Marketing.
  • Support major analyst evaluations. Help prepare submissions, demos and references for influential industry reports. Make sure Sprout Social is represented accurately and well.
  • Leadership/Exec support: Work closely with leadership in developing presentations they can deliver to influential analysts.
  • Bring analyst insight back into Sprout Social. Capture what analysts say about our market and our competitors. Share it with Product, Marketing and leadership.
  • Keep the calendar and the record. Track analyst report cycles, deadlines and follow-up actions so nothing slips.

What you’ll bring

The minimum qualifications for this role include:

  • 5+ years of experience in product marketing, competitive intelligence, analyst relations, market research or a similar role in business-to-business (B2B) software.
  • Strong research skills. You can dig through product releases, reviews, filings and news, and separate signals from noise.
  • Strategic communicator. Proactively deliver tailored market intelligence, trend updates, and high-impact recommendations to senior leadership and cross-functional teams.
  • Strong AI skills. You use AI tools and large language models (LLMs) every day to research, analyze and create. You can turn one-off work into repeatable AI workflows that others use.
  • Live deal enablement. Demonstrated experience supporting active B2B sales cycles through direct competitive deal consulting and live enablement.

Preferred qualifications for this role include:

  • Knowledge of the social media management, social listening or media intelligence market.
  • Experience with competitive intelligence tools.
  • Experience working with analyst firms, or supporting evaluations such as a Magic Quadrant or a Wave.
  • Experience creating sales enablement materials such as battle cards.

How you’ll grow

Within 1 month, you’ll plant your roots, including:

  • Complete Sprout Social’s new hire training & onboarding program alongside other new Sprout team members. You’ll gain a broader understanding of our products and how your role fits into the organization.
  • Meet your stakeholders across R&D, Product Marketing, Sales and CS.
  • Get to know our competitor set and our current intelligence sources and materials.
  • Review our analyst relationships, upcoming report cycles and past evaluations.
  • Start product onboarding, become familiar with our suite of products.

Within 3 months, you’ll start hitting your stride by:

  • Publish your first competitive intelligence reports on a regular schedule.
  • Deliver your first rapid-response analysis of a competitor release.
  • Support your first live competitive deal alongside a Sales rep.
  • Join analyst briefings and take ownership of scheduling and preparation.

Within 6 months, you’ll be making a clear impact through:

  • Run the competitive intelligence program end to end, from monitoring to reporting.
  • Refresh battle cards and competitive materials for our key competitor set.
  • Manage an analyst evaluation submission with support from your manager.
  • Partner with the GTM Systems and Applied AI team to build your first AI-powered intelligence workflow.

Within 12 months, you’ll make this role your own by:

  • Be the recognized expert on our competitors inside Sprout Social.
  • Influence product and go-to-market decisions with your intelligence work.
  • Own our analyst relations calendar and strengthen our position in major reports.
  • Systemize competitive intelligence across the company, so every team works from the same current information.

Of course what is outlined above is the ideal timeline, but things may shift based on business needs and other projects and tasks could be added at the discretion of your manager.

Our Benefits Program

We’re proud to regularly be recognized for our team, product, and culture. We invest in our team with a comprehensive, competitive benefits program:

  • Comprehensive Health & Wellness: Premium BCBSIL medical, dental (high/low plans), and vision (Eyemed) insurance for you and your eligible dependents.
  • Premium Mental Health Support: Full, free access to Modern Health for you and your dependents, including coaching, therapy sessions, and digital wellness resources.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with a 50% company match on your first 6% of contributions (a 3% total match).
  • Financial Security: 100% employer-paid Life and Disability insurance for your peace of mind.
  • Flexible Paid Time Off: A flexible PTO policy, supplemented with additional company-wide Rest & Recharge days throughout the year.
  • Paid Parental Leave: Up to 16 weeks of paid leave for new parents to support you in expanding your family.
  • Annual Lifestyle Stipend: A $1,000 USD annual Lifestyle Spending Account to spend on your physical, mental, and financial well-being.
  • Work From Home Support: A one-time $550 USD stipend to set up your home office, plus a monthly $50 USD stipend for internet.
  • Giving Back: 16 hours of paid volunteer time annually, plus a $100 annual match for your charitable donations.
  • Additional Financial Perks: Access to pre-tax commuter benefits, subsidized child/eldercare (Care.com), discounted pet insurance (Figo), and no-cost personalized financial wellness support through Your Money Line.

*This list is for informational purposes only. Benefit offerings are discretionary and subject to change and do not constitute a contract or guarantee of benefits.

Whenever possible, Sprout wants to provide our team with the flexibility to work in the location that makes the most sense for them. Sprout maintains a remote workforce in many places in the United States. However, we are not set up in all states, so please look at the drop-down box in our application to see whether your state is listed. Few roles require an office setting. If your position requires a physical presence in a Sprout office, it will be evident in the job listing and your offer letter.

Our salary ranges reflect the expected earning potential for this role. Individual pay is based on geographic zone, relevant experience, and skills.

Our current hiring range for this role: $94,400.00 – $118,000.00 annually. Offers are made within this range, with opportunities to grow within the broader band based on performance and impact.

We share both our current hiring range and our broader geographic salary bands to provide transparency into our compensation philosophy. This ensures you understand not only your starting potential but also the long-term growth potential available as you progress in your role.

We have two geographic pay zones in the United States:

Zone 1 (New York, California, Washington): $103,800.00-$155,800.00

Zone 2 (All other US states): $94,400.00 – $141,600.00

These ranges were determined by a market-based compensation approach; we used data from trusted third-party compensation sources to set equitable, consistent, and competitive ranges. We also evaluate compensation bi-annually, identify any changes in the market and make adjustments to our ranges and existing employee compensation as needed.

Base pay is only one element of an employee's total compensation at Sprout. Every Sprout team member has an opportunity to receive restricted stock units (RSUs) under Sprout’s equity plan. Employees (and their dependents) are covered by medical, dental, vision, basic life, accidental death, and dismemberment insurance, and Modern Health (a wellness benefit). Employees are able to enroll in Sprout’s company’s 401k plan, in which Sprout will match 50% of your contributions up to 6% with a maximum contribution. Sprout offers “Flexible Paid Time Off” and ten paid holidays. We have outlined the various components to an employee’s full compensation package here to help you to understand our total rewards package.

jobs.description:
Position Purpose:
Supports Enterprise Privacy & Security Risk Management (EPSRM) and other teams across Centene by translating complex regulatory, legislative, and contractual requirements into actionable, risk-informed analysis and advisory-ready outputs, among other duties.

Serves as a critical execution layer within the Privacy & Security Enterprise Engagement model, working as part of a team of Lead Analysts that support both Market Enterprise Engagement Officers (EEOs) and Shared Services EEOs. Reviews and interprets contracts, laws, regulations, and industry frameworks to determine Centene's obligations related to privacy, security, artificial intelligence (AI) governance, and operational resilience.

Operating in a Second Line of Defense (2LoD) advisory capacity, this role enables EEOs to focus on stakeholder engagement and decision-making by delivering high-quality analysis, requirement traceability, and executive-ready insights. Applies deep subject matter expertise, operates with limited oversight, and influences cross-functional stakeholders to ensure regulatory and contractual requirements are effectively operationalized across the enterprise.

  • Analyzes and interprets federal/state laws, regulations, and contractual obligations (e.g., state contracts, DPAs, security addenda) to identify requirements impacting operations, systems, and data, and maintain awareness of evolving regulatory landscapes (CMS, HIPAA, state programs, AI governance).
  • Translates regulatory and contractual requirements into structured, enforceable, and testable obligations aligned to enterprise frameworks (e.g., NIST, CMS/MARSE/ARC-AMPE, NCQA), including development and maintenance of requirement inventories, mappings, and traceability artifacts linking controls, owners, and evidence.
  • Performs impact assessments and support regulatory change management to evaluate the effect of new or changing requirements across business and technology environments, including maintaining regulatory tracking mechanisms and GRC inputs to support enterprise visibility.
  • Acts as a core support partner to EEOs and enterprise stakeholders, delivering risk-informed insights, recommendations, and updates on regulatory developments, compliance posture, and mitigation strategies.
  • Develops executive-ready outputs (e.g., briefings, dashboards, summaries, risk analyses) to support decision-making and communicate complex requirements in a clear, actionable manner.
  • Supports the development of playbooks, templates, and standard operating procedures (SOPs), and identify opportunities to enhance processes, tools, and analytical methods to drive consistency and efficiency.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
  • Complies with all policies and standards.

Education/Experience:
Bachelor's Degree Information Security, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Public Policy, Legal/Paralegal Studies, or related field; or equivalent experience required.

Master's Degree preferred.

Juris Doctor (JD) preferred.

  • Experience producing executive-ready communications and advisory materials, influencing business and technical stakeholders without direct authority, and supporting risk-informed decision-making within a Second Line of Defense (2LoD) advisory model in complex, cross-functional environments preferred.
  • Experience applying healthcare regulatory frameworks (e.g., CMS, HIPAA, state Medicaid/Exchange requirements, NCQA) and security/privacy control frameworks (e.g., NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, CMS/MARSE/ARC-AMPE) within compliance, risk, or technology environments preferred.

Licenses/Certifications:
CISSP, CISM, CRISC, or similar information security or risk certification preferred.

Privacy, AI Governance or compliance-related certifications (e.g., CIPP, CIPM, AIGP, etc.) preferred.

jobs.excerpt: We're transforming the grocery industryAt Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together.
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Why this role is on the menu

Media is one of Instacart's most powerful growth levers, and the team is actively evolving its operating model to serve multiple lines of business through a mix of in-house and agency-managed media. Without strong operating infrastructure, the media team risks spending its time on coordination and manual workarounds rather than strategy, innovation, and campaign performance. This role exists to design, own, and continuously improve the core mechanics of how the media team plans, executes, and optimizes work. Twelve months from now, the media team will operate with a clear, scalable, and trusted operating system that makes it easy to do great work without reliance on tribal knowledge.

What you'll cook up in your first year

  • Media's planning frameworks, templates, and cadences are redesigned and adopted across the team, driving clarity and accountability in annual and quarterly planning cycles.
  • A scalable media operating system is in place: budget pacing, performance reporting, campaign enablement, and process automation are governed by clear standards and a maintained roadmap.
  • Intake, automation, and workflow tooling are simplified and reliable, with manual double-entry eliminated through well-scoped AI and automation solutions.
  • Cross-functional operating rhythms, including business reviews and integrated campaign program management, run with transparent workback schedules, strong stakeholder communication, and consistent follow-through.
  • Change management for new systems and processes is executed effectively, with documentation, training, and communication plans that drive adoption across media and partner teams.

The secret ingredients we're looking for

Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications)

  • 7 to 10 or more years of experience in Marketing or Media Operations, Program Management, Business Operations, or a closely related field within complex, cross-functional organizations.
  • Demonstrated experience as a senior individual contributor with real decision authority and ownership over cross-functional operating systems.
  • Fluency in program management: workback schedules, risk management, project velocity, and hands-on ownership of project management tooling for non-technical teams.
  • Systems mindset: proven ability to take fragmented or inconsistent processes and make them clearer, simpler, and more reliable, with a track record of building standardized templates and driving adoption across multiple teams.
  • Strong understanding of how media teams plan, intake, prioritize, and execute work at scale, including familiarity with media tech stacks.
  • Excellent written communication and structured thinking, with the ability to turn complex inputs into crisp narratives and leadership-ready materials.
  • Analytical fluency: comfortable working with performance metrics and basic financial concepts, and able to pressure-test assumptions and identify gaps.

Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Practical experience using automation and AI tools to streamline workflows, such as meeting prep, intake triage, and template population.
  • Experience in retail, consumer tech, or marketplace businesses.

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. jobs.excerpt: Our client is a global leader in fire protection, delivering advanced fire detection and fire suppression solutions for mission-critical environments where uptime, asset protection, and operational resilience are paramount.
jobs.description:
Our client is a global leader in fire protection, delivering advanced fire detection and fire suppression solutions for mission-critical environments where uptime, asset protection, and operational resilience are paramount. Their technologies are trusted worldwide across commercial, industrial, infrastructure, and high-risk sectors.

Within the rapidly expanding data centre sector, our client provides integrated fire safety solutions specifically engineered to protect critical digital infrastructure, minimise downtime, and safeguard people and assets. Their systems combine ultra-early warning detection, intelligent control technologies, and highly effective suppression solutions tailored for white space environments, electrical rooms, battery energy storage systems, UPS rooms, generator halls, and associated plant areas.

On the detection side, the company offers advanced smoke detection, aspirating smoke detection, heat detection, intelligent alarm panels, and integrated monitoring platforms that enable immediate identification of fire events and rapid response.

On the suppression side, they provide sprinkler systems, clean agent systems, water mist technologies, foam systems, pumps, valves, flow-switches, and associated special hazard solutions designed to meet the unique requirements of modern data centre facilities.

Renowned for engineering excellence, innovation, and compliance with international standards, our client is a preferred partner to some of the world's most demanding customers.

Job Purpose

The European Area Business Development Manager – Data Centres will lead the strategic growth of the company's fire detection and fire suppression business across the European data centre sector.

This role is focused on winning new business, developing key strategic relationships, influencing specifications, and positioning the company as a preferred fire protection partner across hyperscale, colocation, enterprise, and edge data centre projects throughout Europe.

The successful candidate will possess a strong understanding of the European data centre ecosystem, including developers, owners, consultants, contractors, and operators, together with the ability to manage complex technical sales cycles and long-term strategic opportunities.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute a European growth strategy focused specifically on the data centre vertical.

Drive sales of both fire detection and fire suppression solutions into new-build and retrofit data centre projects.

Identify, qualify, and convert new business opportunities with hyperscalers, colocation providers, enterprise operators, and developers.

Build strong relationships with key stakeholders including consultants, EPC firms, MEP consultants, general contractors, system integrators, and end-users.

Secure product specifications at design stage through engagement with engineering consultants and project stakeholders.

Position the company as a strategic technical partner for mission-critical fire protection solutions.

Manage key accounts across multiple European territories and develop long-term account growth plans.

Work closely with regional distributors and channel partners to maximise market penetration.

Support tender submissions, technical proposals, quotations, and commercial negotiations.

Collaborate with engineering, product management, and operations teams to ensure solutions meet project requirements.

Monitor market trends including data centre construction pipelines, competitor activity, emerging technologies, and regulatory developments.

Represent the business at major industry exhibitions, conferences, and sector events across Europe.

Prepare accurate sales forecasts, pipeline reports, budgets, and strategic updates for senior management.

Maintain strong CRM discipline and opportunity management processes.

Carry out any other duties as reasonably requested.

Required Skills & Abilities

Strong commercial hunter mentality with proven business development success.

Deep understanding of the European data centre market and decision-making landscape.

Excellent relationship-building skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.

Strong technical aptitude in fire detection, suppression, or mission-critical building systems.

Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.

Ability to manage long and complex sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders.

High level of commercial acumen and strategic thinking.

Strong organisational and time management skills.

Analytical mindset with strong problem-solving capability.

Ability to work independently within a remote structure.

Willingness to travel extensively across Europe.

Fluency in English essential; additional European languages highly desirable.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 10 years' commercial experience in business development or sales.

Strong track record selling into the data center sector, ideally within fire protection, MEP, HVAC, electrical, security, or critical infrastructure solutions.

Existing network across European data center owners, developers, consultants, and contractors strongly preferred.

Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, or related discipline preferred.

Experience using CRM platforms such as Salesforce.

Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.

Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time.

Work Environment & Benefits

Remote / home-based role with significant European travel.

Opportunity to join a high-growth global leader in a rapidly expanding sector.

Competitive base salary with uncapped performance incentives.

Executive-level career progression opportunities.

International and collaborative working environment.

Inclusive culture that values diversity, innovation, and performance.

jobs.description:
We are seeking a strategic, experienced, and hands-on Assistant Vice Presidentof Procurement to lead Symetra's enterprise procurement function and serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior leaders across the organization. This leader will balance long-term strategy with day-to-day execution, ensuring Procurement delivers measurable business value, strong governance, and an excellent experience for the business.

About the role

In this role, you will lead all aspects of the enterprise procurement function, including policies, processes, sourcing, contracting, supplier management, and procurement technology. You will partner with Law, Finance, Technology, Risk, Information Security, Vendor Management, and business leaders to establish effective enterprise procurement practices, governance, and controls. You will set functional strategy and priorities while creating an operating model that enables the team to deliver strategic value and responsive day-to-day execution.

What You will Do

  • Staff Management: Recruit and develop strategic procurement staff to be a high-performing and motivated team responsible for collaborating with business and supplier partners. Build capability, establish clear accountability and decision rights, develop the leadership bench, and create a culture of ownership, collaboration, continuous improvement, and service.
  • Process & Operational Excellence: Identify and implement the metrics, tools, processes, and controls needed to optimize procurement performance. Lead end-to-end improvement across intake, sourcing, contracting, renewals, and supplier management, balancing speed, user experience, business needs, risk, and control. Establish clear performance expectations and use data to manage pipeline, backlog, cycle time, renewals, productivity, adoption, and other measures that demonstrate results.
  • Business Strategy & Category Management: Lead the development and execution of enterprise procurement strategy aligned to Symetra's growth and business priorities. Establish category and sourcing strategies across key spend areas, identify opportunities for supplier consolidation and demand management, and translate enterprise priorities into a multi-year Procurement roadmap with clear objectives, priorities, and accountability.
  • Enterprise Supplier Strategy & Governance: Establish a holistic enterprise view of strategic and multi-use supplier relationships, including spend, contracts and SOWs, renewals, performance, risk, obligations, and commercial opportunities. Lead supplier strategy, performance management, executive business reviews, and relationship governance while ensuring appropriate contractual protections, risk mitigation, business continuity considerations, and escalation processes are embedded throughout the supplier lifecycle.
  • Executive & Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner with senior leaders to align Procurement priorities with enterprise strategy and business needs. Build strong relationships across Law, Finance, Technology, Information Security, Risk, Vendor Management, and the divisions; influence decisions, resolve complex issues, and establish clear roles, handoffs, and decision rights across the procurement lifecycle.
  • Transformation & Technology: Lead the modernization of Procurement, including the procurement platform and other procurement technology, data, analytics, and workflow capabilities. Drive process standardization, change management, and sustainable improvements in cycle time, visibility, user experience, compliance, and value realization.
  • Value Creation & Financial Management: Establish and deliver measurable Procurement value through savings, cost avoidance, demand management, supplier consolidation, contract optimization, and process efficiency. Establish credible baselines, track benefits, and communicate Procurement's financial and business impact to executive leadership.

What Success Looks Like

  • Procurement is viewed as a trusted enterprise partner that enables business growth, delivers measurable value, and protects Symetra through strong commercial and supplier governance.
  • The function operates with clear priorities, decision rights, processes, metrics, and accountability, providing transparency and a consistent experience across the enterprise.
  • The Procurement transformation and technology roadmap is executed with strong adoption and sustainable improvements in efficiency, visibility, user experience, control, and supplier value.
  • The Procurement team is high-performing and well-developed, with the capabilities, leadership, and operating discipline needed to scale with Symetra's growth while maintaining confidence among senior leaders.

Why Work at Symetra

Here’s what some of our employees have to say about why they work at Symetra:

“If you want to invest in yourself and build a career, this is a great place to work. If you don't want to put in the effort to learn the industry and become a student of the business (it takes real effort!), there are easier places to work.” - Cris H., VP Internal Sales

“We're big enough to make an impact on the country, but small enough to care and know who you are and what you're contributing to the organization. All new ideas are welcome!” - Stephanie F., VP Customer Service & Operations

What we offer you

Benefits and Perks

We don’t take a “one-size-fits-all” approach when it comes to our employees. Our programs are designed to make your life better both at work and at home.

  • Flexible full-time or hybrid telecommuting arrangements
  • Plan for your future with our 401(k) plan and take advantage of immediate vesting and company matching up to 6%
  • Paid time away including vacation and sick time, flex days and ten paid holidays
  • Give back to your community and double your impact through our company matching
  • Want more details? Check out ourSymetra Benefits Overview

Compensation

Salary Range: $141,600 - $236,000 plus eligibility for annual bonus program and long-term incentive plan

Who You Are

  • 10+ years of progressive procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, or related experience, including progressive leadership responsibility for a complex enterprise procurement function
  • 5+ years of people leadership experience, with demonstrated success building and developing high-performing teams
  • Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior executives
  • Strategic problem solver with hands-on execution capability and outstanding attention to detail who is comfortable operating at both the strategic and tactical levels
  • The ability to navigate complexity, lead several priorities, and deliver under tight deadlines while creating clarity, accountability, and momentum

  • Significant experience in contract negotiation and administration, strategic sourcing, supplier relationship management, and commercial value creation
  • Experience working in a highly regulated industry, financial services, insurance, or a similarly complex environment is preferred.

About This Opportunity

We are a property management company looking to bring on another remote team member to support our accounting and administrative operations. This role is primarily focused on accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general accounting work — with approximately one-third of the time dedicated to property management administrative tasks.

Here is how we think about this hire: we are not looking for a resume. We are looking for a person. We hire the same way across our team — remote or in-office — and the standard is intelligence, energy, and the ability to learn fast. Most people who join us start with the basics: processing invoices and general admin. That is the entry point, not the ceiling. If you pick it up quickly and can handle more complex work, we move you up and bring someone new in to cover the basics.

What You Will Start With

Every new team member starts here. This is the foundation, and we take it seriously.

  • Process vendor and contractor invoices accurately and in a timely manner — this is the primary entry-point task
  • Assist with accounts payable and accounts receivable functions, ensuring transactions are recorded correctly
  • Support general accounting data entry and file maintenance
  • Handle property management administrative tasks — approximately one-third of your time — including document management, communication support, and operational coordination
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with internal team members and external vendors or tenants as needed

Where This Role Goes

For the right person, this is not a static position. As you demonstrate accuracy, reliability, and the ability to handle more complex work, your responsibilities will expand. That might include:

  • Full-cycle AP/AR management across a property portfolio

• Bank and account reconciliations

  • Financial reporting and month-end support
  • Deeper property management accounting functions — tenant billing, owner reporting, trust accounting
  • Taking on higher-complexity work as the company continues to grow and hire

What We Are Looking For

  • Intelligence and high energy — this is the baseline for everyone we hire, remote or otherwise
  • A genuine ability and willingness to learn — you pick things up quickly, ask good questions, and apply feedback immediately
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal — you are clear, professional, and responsive
  • Detail orientation and accuracy — invoice processing and accounting work require getting it right every time
  • Willingness to start with the basics and earn your way into more complex responsibilities
  • Self-directed and reliable in a remote environment — you manage your own workload without needing constant oversight

Accounting & Property Management Experience

Experience is welcome but not required. Here is how we look at it:

  • No experience — if you are sharp, high-energy, and learn fast, we will train you on everything
  • Some accounting or administrative experience — a great foundation that will shorten your ramp-up time
  • Experienced candidates with AP/AR, property management, or accounting backgrounds — welcome and will be compensated accordingly, provided you are willing to start with foundational tasks and grow from there
  • Property management experience is a meaningful plus — familiarity with vendor management, tenant communication, or property accounting will help you contribute more quickly

• Licensed CPA

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You are the kind of person who figures things out — you do not wait to be told every step
  • Your invoices are processed accurately and on time, every time
  • You communicate clearly and professionally whether you are emailing a vendor or updating a spreadsheet
  • You see the basics not as beneath you but as the foundation everything else is built on
  • You are ready to grow — and when the opportunity comes, you are already prepared for it

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

At Salesforce, we believe that AI requires a trusted context. Join our Data Foundation Pre-Sales team as a Data Architect helping clients envision the transformation of their businesses through Data platform offerings coming from Informatica and MuleSoft and focussing on Data and AI within Salesforce.

The Role

As a Data Architect, you will act as a trusted advisor to our customers, leveraging your deep technical expertise in data governance, cataloguing, data quality and data infrastructure to guide them through Informatica and MuleSoft solutions. Working closely with Account Executives, Solution Engineers and C-level leaders throughout the end-to-end sales cycle, you will use your strong presentation and solutioning skills to navigate complex accounts. By aligning technical and architectural requirements with customer business drivers, strategy, and funding, you will qualify opportunities and ensure our customers realize the platform's full value.

You will support the customer enterprise architects and domain architects to build an Architectural Vision and to-be Architecture for Digital and Data Transformation, with a clear positioning of the value of Informatica and MuleSoft in this vision.   • Impactful Work: Work at the forefront of AI and data innovation, directly helping enterprises solve complex compliance, governance, and architecture challenges.

  • In Your First 30–60 Days: You'll complete onboarding, pair with senior teammates on customer opportunities, get certified on core Data Foundation products.

  • Storytelling & Architectural Advisory: Strong experience partnering collaboratively with Sales and Solutions Engineering teams during the sales process, providing crucial architectural guidance to support the creation of compelling demos that clearly illustrate immediate ROI and practical application for diverse stakeholders.
  • Workshop Facilitation & Strategic Alignment: Expertise in orchestrating inclusive, targeted technical workshops to guide key decisions and align architectural best practices with the customer's core business priorities.

Bonus Experience (Desired, Not Required):

Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the systems that drive core auction understanding and marketplace balance within our Ads Quality domain. This is a high-impact, technically complex space where your work will directly influence the health of the ads ecosystem — from how auctions are structured and optimized to how quality signals inform ranking and relevance. You'll partner closely with a team of talented machine learning engineers and ads engineers who are building at the frontier of what's possible in retail media.

If you're energized by ambiguous, high-stakes problems, fluent in the language of ML and online advertising, and eager to accelerate experimentation in a fast-moving environment — this is the role for you.

About the Job

  • Own the product vision and roadmap for ads quality systems, including auction mechanics, marketplace balance, and the signals that govern ad ranking and relevance across Instacart's retail media network.
  • Drive the strategy and execution for increasing the velocity of experimentation across the ads quality team — designing frameworks that allow the team to test, learn, and iterate faster without sacrificing rigor or integrity.
  • Work hands-on with machine learning engineers and ads engineers to translate complex ML model outputs and auction dynamics into clear product requirements, hypotheses, and measurable outcomes.
  • Define and track the right success metrics for ads quality, navigating tradeoffs between advertiser performance, shopper experience, and marketplace health — and communicating those tradeoffs clearly to senior stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Product Marketing Manager - Public Sector
jobs.excerpt: Who we areSamsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's Connected Operations platform helps organizations that depend on physical operations — fleets, construction, utilities, public works, and first responders — run safer, more efficiently, and more sustainably.

We're looking for a Sr. Manager, Product Marketing Manager, Public Sector to own the narrative, positioning, and enablement that will define how Samsara wins in government. You'll be the team's expert on how public sector buyers evaluate technology — from the contract vehicles they procure through, to the compliance bar they hold vendors to, to the mission outcomes they're ultimately accountable for.

This is a strategic, cross-functional role for someone who already understands government and frameworks like FedRAMP and StateRAMP/GovRAMP. The ideal candidate is someone who wants to build a public sector product marketing motion, not just execute inside one that already exists.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the U.S. We prefer candidates based in or near Washington, D.C., or those able to work Eastern time zone hours.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your work will have real-world stakes — helping public agencies keep roads plowed, fleets safe, and essential services running for the communities they serve.
  • You're fluent in how the government buys technology: You understand procurement cycles, contract vehicles, and compliance frameworks well enough to turn them into a go-to-market advantage rather than a blocker.
  • You're energized by building, not just executing: Samsara's federal go-to-market motion is still being defined — you'll have real ownership over the frameworks, positioning, and playbooks that shape it.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won't be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You'll be surrounded by a high-caliber team that pushes you to do your best work.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead as a player-coach: Manage a direct report while helping build the public sector PMM team's foundation — sharing in the strategic work, coaching for growth, and creating the frameworks that enable the function to scale.
  • Own public sector positioning and messaging: Develop and evolve Samsara's core narrative for government buyers across federal, state, local, and education segments — grounded in mission outcomes rather than generic product benefits
  • Build Samsara's federal go-to-market foundation: Partner cross-functionally to define how Samsara approaches the federal market, including messaging and enablement that reflect our compliance roadmap as it evolves
  • Translate compliance into a sales advantage: Understand the FedRAMP authorization process and impact levels — deeply enough to explain it clearly to sales teams and prospects, and to inform internal conversations about authorization strategy and timing
  • Drive product and platform launches for public sector: Localize Samsara's launches for a government audience, ensuring messaging reflects agency use cases, procurement realities, and compliance considerations
  • Enable sales and channel teams: Build battlecards, objection-handling guides, RFP/RFI response content, and compliance-focused sales collateral that helps account teams and channel partners win competitive government deals
  • Support competitive intelligence for public sector: Track how competitors position themselves to government buyers, and translate that intelligence into differentiated Samsara messaging and sales guidance
  • Represent Samsara at public sector events and forums: Support flagship industry events and partner conferences with content, speaking support, and thought leadership

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 7+ years of product marketing (or closely related go-to-market) experience, with a meaningful portion of that focused on public sector / government technology marketing (B2G)
  • Working knowledge of the FedRAMP authorization process, and general familiarity with adjacent compliance frameworks (e.g., StateRAMP/GovRAMP, NIST 800-53), with the ability to translate them into clear guidance for internal teams
  • Proven ability to independently own strategic programs from conception to completion, and to influence cross-functional partners without direct authority
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills — able to translate complex topics into clear, compelling narratives for technical and non-technical audiences alike
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience managing a direct report or small team is strongly preferred
  • Direct experience supporting a company through a FedRAMP or StateRAMP/GovRAMP authorization process
  • Experience marketing connected devices, hardware-enabled, or physical-operations software platforms
  • Prior experience in government or a public sector-focused vendor or agency role
  • Established relationships within the Carahsoft ecosystem or with other public sector aggregators/resellers
  • Experience building a public sector or new-market go-to-market motion from scratch — including positioning frameworks and playbooks designed to scale beyond your own work

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$119,297.50—$210,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.
