What You Can Expect

This is a hands-on technical leadership role at the center of how Zoom gets found, understood, and surfaced across both traditional search engines and emerging AI-powered discovery platforms. You will own the technical SEO foundation across a complex, multi-platform web ecosystem spanning Optimizely CMS, WordPress, custom web applications, and modern frontend frameworks, translating search strategy into scalable production solutions. Working closely with SEO and Website Engineering leadership, you will drive high-impact implementations, build reusable SEO capabilities and automation, and establish the engineering standards that keep Zoom's digital presence ahead of the curve. Your work connects directly to organic visibility, pipeline, and revenue, and your fingerprints will be on the architecture decisions that shape how Zoom shows up across Google, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and the next generation of agentic web experiences.

About the Team


You will be part of Zoom's Website Engineering team within the Online Business organization, a cross-functional group of web engineers, CMS specialists, SEO and AEO experts, and performance engineers who build and scale the technical foundation powering Zoom's global web presence. The team collaborates closely with Marketing, Product, Design, Content, and Localization to deliver fast, accessible, and AI-ready digital experiences. Technical excellence, a bias toward automation, and engineering-by-design are at the core of how we operate.

Responsibilities


  • Lead the technical SEO roadmap and execution across Zoom's global web ecosystem, owning high-priority initiatives driven by SEO analysis, audits, crawl data, search performance data, server logs, technical root-cause analysis, and business priorities.
  • Translate SEO and AEO requirements into technical designs, development specifications, production implementations, and ongoing maintenance across Optimizely CMS, WordPress, custom web applications, APIs, and modern frontend frameworks, ensuring requirements are incorporated throughout the software development lifecycle.
  • Own technical solutions for crawlability, indexability, XML sitemaps, robots.txt, canonicalization, redirects, URL architecture, metadata, structured data, internal linking, hreflang, JavaScript rendering, client-side rendering, server-side rendering, static generation, incremental rendering, and search-friendly application architecture.
  • Build and scale reusable SEO capabilities including centralized metadata services, automated sitemap generation, structured-data components, redirect services, internal-linking systems, and standardized SEO configurations that platforms can inherit without repeated manual intervention.
  • Drive Core Web Vitals and web performance improvements, including LCP, INP, CLS, JavaScript execution, rendering performance, image optimization, font loading, third-party scripts, caching, CDN configuration, API performance, and server response times.
  • Develop automated testing, monitoring, dashboards, CI/CD quality gates, proactive alerting, and validation scripts that detect technical SEO issues and prevent regressions from reaching production across broken links, metadata, canonicalization, structured data, redirects, sitemaps, indexability, robots directives, duplicate URLs, internal linking, accessibility, performance, and rendering.
  • Establish the technical foundation for AEO and AI search by implementing structured data, semantic HTML, machine-readable metadata, entity and product schemas, and machine-readable endpoints; evaluate emerging AI-search and agentic-web standards and translate them into practical engineering requirements.
  • Define and maintain technical SEO standards and governance across Optimizely, WordPress, and custom applications, serving as the technical authority for SEO implementation within Web Engineering through reference architectures, launch-readiness criteria, design reviews, and code reviews.
  • Partner with SEO, Content, Product Marketing, Web Engineering, Product, and senior stakeholders to translate search strategy and business priorities into scalable technical solutions, improve Zoom's discoverability and representation across traditional search engines and AI-powered discovery platforms, and connect technical SEO initiatives to measurable organic visibility, acquisition, pipeline, and revenue outcomes.

What We're Looking For


  • 8+ years of experience in technical SEO, web engineering, or a related discipline, with a demonstrated track record leading technical SEO initiatives across large-scale websites and web applications in a B2B SaaS or enterprise technology environment; ability to connect technical SEO work directly to measurable organic visibility, acquisition, pipeline, and revenue outcomes.
  • Deep expertise in technical SEO fundamentals: crawlability, indexation, rendering, canonicalization, redirects, URL architecture, XML sitemaps, robots directives, structured data, internal linking, hreflang, and JavaScript-based web applications; hands-on proficiency with JavaScript, PHP, HTML, and CSS to diagnose and implement technical SEO fixes directly in the codebase and CMS, not only through engineering handoffs.
  • Proven experience improving web performance and Core Web Vitals, including diagnosing issues related to JavaScript execution, rendering, caching, CDN configuration, images, third-party scripts, APIs, and server performance.
  • Experience building scalable SEO capabilities, automation, monitoring, and CI/CD quality gates across enterprise CMS platforms such as Optimizely and WordPress; comfortable going directly into the CMS or codebase to implement configurations, standardize templates, and deploy SEO capabilities across multiple sites and applications without requiring a dedicated engineering sprint for every change.
  • Strong understanding of structured data, Schema.org, JSON-LD, semantic HTML, and the technical foundations required for AEO and AI-powered search, with familiarity with emerging AI search platforms including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews.
  • Strong analytical skills using tools such as Google Search Console, Screaming Frog, Semrush, Ahrefs, Sitebulb, analytics platforms, and application observability tools; experienced in analyzing server logs and crawl logs to identify crawl blocks, indexation gaps, rendering failures, and visibility issues across Google, AI search platforms, and LLM crawlers, and translating those findings into prioritized, actionable fixes.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to influence engineering architecture, establish technical standards, and partner effectively with SEO, Web Engineering, Product, Marketing, Content, and senior stakeholders.

Job title Remote Resourcer, Education (known internally as Remote Worker)

Works alongside Education consultants across SEND, Primary, Secondary and School Facilities
Location Fully remote, working from a private home office outside the UK
Hours 08:00 – 16:30
Model 180 recruitment, candidate side only.
Purpose of the role
The Remote Resourcer owns the candidate journey from first contact to the point a candidate is fully compliant, interviewed, briefed and ready to work. The consultant then takes that candidate to market and manages the client relationship. Every candidate this role produces will be placed into a school setting, so the quality of the screening and the accuracy of the compliance file directly affect the safety of children and the reputation of the business. This is a role where getting the detail right matters more than moving quickly.
Key responsibilities
Candidate attraction and sourcing
▪ Source teaching, teaching assistant, SEND and support staff candidates through job boards, the CRM database, social media, referrals and advertising.
▪ Write and post role adverts that reflect live demand from the consultants you support.
▪ Run daily proactive outreach by phone, email and message to build a pipeline ahead of demand rather than in reaction to it.
▪ Re engage lapsed and dormant candidates already held in the CRM.
▪ Keep a live map of candidate availability by location, phase, subject and specialism.
Screening and interviewing
▪ Carry out a structured telephone initial call then a video registration call following a set interview structure.
▪ Establish and record full employment history, including the reason for any gap of more than one month.
▪ Assess suitability for the setting: experience, phase, behaviour management, SEND experience, safeguarding awareness and motivation.
▪ Confirm availability, travel radius, pay expectations and any restrictions.
▪ Decline unsuitable candidates promptly and professionally, and record the reason.
Compliance and vetting
▪ Verify identity and address using original or certified documentation to the standard set out in the compliance procedure.
▪ Confirm the right to work in the UK and record document type, expiry and share code where applicable.
▪ Process an enhanced DBS check with a children’s barred list check, or verify a suitable existing certificate registered with the DBS Update Service, and carry out a status check.
▪ Complete prohibition from teaching, prohibition from management (section 128) and any sanction or restriction checks required for the role.
▪ Obtain and verify a minimum of two references covering the most recent employment involving children, taken up in writing from a senior person at the organisation and verified by telephone or verified email domain.
▪ Obtain overseas police clearance or a certificate of good conduct for any period lived abroad, in line with the compliance procedure.
▪ Complete an online presence check on shortlisted candidates and record the outcome.
▪ Verify qualifications, QTS status where relevant, and any specialist training certificates.
▪ Obtain a health and medical fitness declaration and escalate anything requiring occupational health input.
▪ Ensure safeguarding, Prevent and any mandatory training is completed and in date before release.
▪ Chase outstanding documents daily and keep the candidate informed of exactly what is still needed.
▪ Maintain compliance records to audit standard so that a file can be produced on request for a client, an inspection or an external audit at any time.
▪ Escalate every discrepancy, gap, unexplained absence or concern to the Remote Team Manager. Never resolve a compliance query by assumption.
Getting candidates work ready
▪ Brief the candidate on how the agency works, expected conduct, dress, timekeeping, absence reporting and safeguarding responsibilities.
▪ Ensure payroll and personal details are set up and correct before the first booking.
▪ Confirm the candidate understands their pay, how timesheets work and who to contact.
▪ Produce a clear, accurate candidate profile or CV in company format that a consultant can send to a client without rework.
▪ Confirm the candidate is genuinely available and still interested before handover.
▪ Ensure all details are in the CRM.
Handover to the consultant
▪ Hand over only candidates who are fully screened, fully compliant and briefed.
▪ Provide the consultant with a short written summary covering suitability, availability, strengths, any client sensitivities and the compliance status.
▪ Answer consultant questions on the candidate and support them with any follow up information required.
▪ Track handed over candidates through to placement and feed back anything learned into future screening.
Systems and administration
▪ Record every call, message, document, interview and decision in the CRM on the day it happens.
▪ Keep candidate records, availability and compliance status accurate at all times. The CRM is the single source of truth.
▪ Maintain the compliance tracker and flag expiring documents before they lapse.
▪ Provide daily and weekly activity reporting to the Remote Team Manager.

jobs.description:
Description

About the Project

We're looking for native-level Spanish (Colombia) speakers with professional voice recording experience to join the Hydrus Project.

The project consists of two scheduled recording sessions from their own home studio.

Because the recordings go straight into production, the audition validates two things equally: your voice and your recording environment.

What You'll Do

  • Audition with two 30 second samples using your home studio set up
  • Once approved, you will complete two scheduled recording sessions of approximately 4 hours each
  • Participate in natural conversation, prompted discussion, and scripted customer-service scenarios
  • Record from your own home studio setup across both sessions

Your Recording Environment

Three things are required, and each is judged separately:

  1. An external microphone: A separate, dedicated microphone is absolutely required — see below.
  2. A dry room: Your voice should sound close and clear, with no echo or hollow, distant quality. Untreated rooms with bare walls, hard floors, and high ceilings usually fail.
  3. A quiet room: No HVAC hum, fans, traffic, appliances, or household noise during recording.

Minimum Required Gear

  • Dynamic Mics (best for untreated rooms): Shure SM58, Shure MV7 / MV7+, RODE PodMic / PodMic USB, or similar.
  • Condenser mic (great in a treated room): RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti / Yeti Orb, Blue Bluebird, Blue Baby Bottle, or similar.
  • Room Treatment: Your recording space should produce studio-quality sound samples – isolation shields, sounds absorbing pads, etc…

Immediately rejected: built-in laptop microphones, phone mics, AirPods, Samsung Buds, headphone-attached mics, headsets, and gaming headsets.

Technical Specification

You must be able to produce audio samples in the meeting the following specifications:

WAV format, 24-bit, 48 kHz, no compression. Free software such as Audacity can produce this. If you cannot export in this format, please do not apply — this level of technicality is required for this role.

Who We're Looking For

  • Native-level Spanish (Colombia) speaker
  • A natural, authentic, friendly, conversational customer-service speaking style
  • A dry, quiet home recording space and a professional microphone, as described above
  • Good background, but not required: Podcasters, youtubers, streamers, recording artists, voice-over actors, etc – anyone who has experience recording audio in a high-quality home studio

Commitment & Compensation

  • Estimated time: approximately 8 hours total across two scheduled sessions
  • Compensation: $35.00 USD per hour

jobs.title: Onboarding & Support Manager
jobs.excerpt: Who are CloudNC? CloudNC is transforming global manufacturing with AI that accelerates CAM programming, maximizes factory output, and empowers machinists to deliver more.
jobs.description:
Who are CloudNC?CloudNC is transforming global manufacturing with AI that accelerates CAM programming, maximizes factory output, and empowers machinists to deliver more.
Our core product, CAM Assist, speeds up CNC machining by tackling the most time-consuming and repetitive parts of the process, from machining strategy to toolpath generation.
It enables machinists to create effective programs in minutes, unlocking their full potential and helping shops increase throughput and improve consistency.
Today, CAM Assist is trusted by over 1,000 machine shops around the world to enhance their teams’ productivity, resolving skills shortages and helping them to deliver efficiently for their customers.
Founded in 2015, CloudNC consists of a world-class team combining expertise in computer science and physical manufacturing, based in our headquarters in London and our factory in Chelmsford.
The technology company is backed by leading venture capital firms Atomico and Episode 1 Ventures, alongside Autodesk and Lockheed Martin as strategic partners.

The short version
We need someone who can get hundreds of machine shops live on CAM Assist without needing a CAM programmer in the room, and who owns product support while they are doing it.

What CAM Assist isAI that writes CNC toolpaths inside the CAM software programmers already use: Mastercam, Fusion, Siemens NX, GibbsCAM and SolidCAM. Work that takes hours takes minutes.
Our customers are precision manufacturers, and they buy it because the time saving is obvious. What sits between signing and seeing that saving is that this is a new product doing something new, on top of the ordinary friction of getting software set up and configured for how that shop works. Closing that gap quickly and repeatably is this job.

What you need to bringYou learn fast. CAM Assist is a new product doing something new, and it moves. You need to get to the point where you can hold your own with an experienced programmer in weeks rather than months, and then do that again every time the product changes. This is the single thing we care most about.
Manufacturing and tooling knowledge. You understand machining, tooling and how a shop actually runs: setups, fixturing, tool libraries, why cycle time is the thing everyone is really talking about. You are familiar with CAM without necessarily having worked as a programmer. Enough to be taken seriously by someone with twenty years on the machines, and enough to know when to bring one of our CAM programmers in.
You are a player-coach. You have managed or mentored people while still carrying real delivery yourself, and you prefer it that way. You will have one direct report to start with and more as we grow, but the job does not become less hands-on as it grows.
Pace. New customers arrive in lumps and the 30-day clock does not care. You need to be comfortable holding fifteen customers at different stages without dropping one, and deciding quickly which of them needs you today.
The instinct to build rather than absorb. Stopping to productise something, instead of doing it manually again, is most of what separates people who are good at this role from people who are merely busy in it.

Useful, but not requiredExperience with manufacturing or engineering software, in support, applications engineering or implementation · hands-on time in any CAM system · experience getting customers live on technical software · running or supervising a support queue · writing help content or building out a knowledge base · working alongside product and engineering on customer issues

The jobYou own two things: getting every new customer live, and the product support function that looks after them afterwards.
This is a hands-on management role, and we mean hands-on. You will be running onboarding calls yourself, in the product, with customers, from your first month and permanently. You will also own product support as an area of the business, including line managing the Product Support Specialist who runs the queue day to day.
Roughly 60% of your week is delivering onboarding yourself, 20% is owning support, and 20% is building the systems that mean the hundredth customer gets live faster than the tenth.
You are not a process manager reviewing other people's work. If you are looking for a role where you delegate the customer conversations, this is not it.
Concretely, you will:
  • Run onboarding personally for new customers, from sales handover through installation and setup to a first real part
  • Own the product support function outright: the queue, the response quality, the escalation path, and the outcome
  • Line manage and develop our Product Support Specialist, and build the team out as we scale
  • Turn recurring friction into playbooks, help content and product requirements, so the same problem stops arriving twice
  • Watch the usage data, spot customers going quiet, and intervene before they stall
  • Manage the customer escalations through support and onboarding into our CAM programming team
What you will be measured on
  • The percentage of new customers reaching first accepted toolpath within 30 days
  • The percentage onboarded in one or two touchpoints, which we want going up
  • The percentage of support requests needing CAM programmer time, which we want going down through process / documentation evolution
  • Support responsiveness, and more importantly the fall in repeat contacts as documentation, tooling and the product improved
Probably not for you ifYou want to spend your day solving the hardest technical problem in the room. That is a CAM programmer's job here, and it is a good one, but it is not this one.
Or if you are looking for a step away from delivery. The management here comes on top of the hands-on work, not instead of it.

How we workSmall team, deliberately, and we lean towards building systems rather than adding people.
Onboarding and product support sit together as one customer experience function, and you will own it. Two separate queues, the same skill set, and a shared job: making the experience of CAM Assist good enough that fewer customers need to ask in the first place. Most support tickets are experience problems rather than technical ones, so the two sides see the same things from different ends.
Fully remote within the US. We are a UK company with a growing US team, and the working week is already built around UK and US overlap, so you will not be the only one on a transatlantic call. Occasional travel for strategic customers, trade shows and team meet-ups.

BenefitsStock Options
Annual Performance Equity Award
36 days of annual leave including public holidays
Leading medical plan
Life Insurance
4 weeks paid Sabbatical every 4 years
401k
Enhanced primary, secondary and adoption parental pay & leave (maternity/paternity)
and more...

Equal Opportunities StatementWe are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, valuing individuality and embracing all people. The success of CloudNC is a result of diversity of thought. We recognise this comes from people truly belonging. We encourage different perspectives and skills to collaborate towards our mission - disrupting the manufacturing industry. We celebrate diversity and continually improve our inclusivity efforts.

Statement of Work (SOW)

Title: Legal Advisory Services for the Transition of Relief International Philippines' Legal Registration and Organizational Affiliation

Location(s) where the Services are to be performed: Philippines

Contracting Manager: Country Director

Timing: 10 days

Dates: September 14, 2026

Pre-Hire Checks Requirements: This role is classified as requiring standard pre-employment checks

About Relief International

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience, and promote long-term health and wellbeing. We work in 16 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, providing Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

Relief International (RI) Philippines operates with a strong focus on peacebuilding, humanitarian response, and development programming in areas affected by conflict, natural disasters, and socio-economic vulnerabilities. Since establishing its presence in the country, RI has worked closely with local communities, civil society organizations, and government institutions to support conflict-affected populations, promote social cohesion, and deliver life-saving assistance. The country's program integrates gender equality, youth empowerment, and community resilience across its portfolio, ensuring that interventions address both immediate needs and long-term structural challenges.

Scope and Nature of Services:

Relief International is exploring to transition its legal registration in the Philippines from its affiliation with Relief International Inc., (US) to Relief International-France (RI-France). The Contractor will provide legal research and advisory services to enable RI Philippines to assess its current Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) registration and organizational structure and determine whether any transition, merger, restructuring, amendment, or other corporate action is legally required or advisable for its affiliation with RI-France.

Key Delivery Milestones

Milestone 1: Inception Briefing Note

Within three (3) calendar days from commencement of the engagement, submit a preliminary briefing note covering:

  • preliminary understanding of RI Philippines’ current SEC registration and corporate structure;
  • key legal questions and issues to be examined;
  • proposed research and assessment approach;
  • list of additional documents or information required from RI; and
  • any immediate matters requiring management clarification.

Milestone 2: Comprehensive Legal Research and Advisory Report

The report shall include an Executive Summary outlining the recommended option(s), indicative timeline, estimated costs, key risks, and management decisions required.

Within five (5) calendar days from acceptance of the inception briefing note , submit a comprehensive report addressing, at minimum:

1. Current Status Assessment

  • review of RI Philippines’ current SEC registration, corporate structure, and governance arrangements;
  • relevant Philippine laws, SEC rules, regulations, issuances, and other regulatory requirements; and
  • legal and compliance implications of maintaining the current structure.

2. Legal Analysis

  • assessment of the viable legal options available to RI and the implications of each option;
  • legally available pathways, including maintaining the current structure, amendment of registration, restructuring, merger, or other applicable options;
  • advantages, disadvantages, legal implications, and key assumptions for each viable option; and
  • implications for governance, board composition, corporate documents, and affiliation with Relief International global entities.

3. Implementation Requirements and Indicative Timeline

  • For each legally viable option, where applicable, provide the major implementation stages, government agencies involved, SEC and other regulatory requirements, documentary requirements, internal approvals, and indicative processing time for each stage.

4. Cost Assessment

  • Provide estimated government, SEC filing, publication, professional/legal, and other anticipated administrative costs, clearly distinguishing confirmed costs, indicative estimates, and costs requiring further verification.

5. Key Implications and Risks

  • governance and board composition implications;
  • implications for corporate registrations, permits, and regulatory compliance;
  • implications for existing contracts and ongoing obligations, where applicable;
  • potential legal, operational, and implementation risks associated with each viable option; and
  • key assumptions, limitations, and matters requiring further verification.

6. Recommendations

  • Provide professional recommendations on the preferred approach, if applicable; priority actions; matters requiring further verification; and critical decisions requiring RI management consideration.

Milestone 3: Presentation

Within two (2) calendar days following submission of the Comprehensive Legal Research and Advisory Report, present the key findings and recommendations to RI management and respond to clarification questions regarding the report. This period also includes revising the report, if necessary.

Payment Terms:

Professional fees shall be as stipulated in the approved engagement proposal and/or contract amendment, subject to applicable taxes. Payment shall be linked to satisfactory completion and acceptance of the agreed deliverables as follows:

Payment Schedule

Initial payment (50%): Upon signing of the engagement and issuance of the required invoice

Required Output: Signed Independent Contractor Agreement and required invoice

Final payment (50%): Upon submission, review, and acceptance by RI of the Comprehensive Legal Research and Advisory Report and completion of the management consultation session

Required Output: Accepted Comprehensive Legal Research and Advisory Report and completed presentation

The remaining payment shall be due only upon satisfactory completion and acceptance of the required deliverables. Where a deliverable does not substantially address the agreed scope, RI may request reasonable clarification or revision before acceptance and payment. The Contractor shall submit the required billing documentation in accordance with RI procedures.

Timeline and Delays

The Contractor shall promptly notify RI of any circumstance that could reasonably affect completion of the agreed deliverables within the stated timeline.

If a deliverable is delayed beyond the agreed due date without prior written agreement from RI, RI reserves the right to withhold final payment until the outstanding deliverable has been completed and accepted.

Information, services or resources to be provided by the Contractor:

The Contractor will provide the following services and resources to complete the assignment:

  • Legal expertise in Philippine corporate, SEC registration, governance, and related regulatory requirements relevant to the assignment.
  • Legal research and analysis based on applicable laws, SEC rules, regulations, issuances, and other authoritative sources.
  • Preparation of a written assessment that clearly identifies the legal basis for material conclusions and distinguishes confirmed information from assumptions, estimates, and matters requiring further verification.
  • Provision of periodic updates and timely requests for documents or clarifications needed from RI.
  • Presentation of findings to RI management and response to reasonable clarification questions relating to the submitted report.

The Contractor will ensure that all work performed under this contract is completed in accordance with Relief International policies on confidentiality and legal documentation handling.

Safeguarding and conduct

  • Uphold and promote RI’s commitment to ensuring the safeguarding and safety of the vulnerable communities we serve.
  • Ensure that your behaviour inside and outside of work promotes the values outlined with RI’s code of conduct and safeguarding policies.
  • Consistent with RI’s safeguarding and protection policies, contribute to ensuring that all those who come into contact with RI staff and the communities we serve can be trusted to work safely with them.

Acceptance Criteria

The engagement will be considered complete when the agreed deliverables have been submitted and accepted by RI. The Comprehensive Legal Research and Advisory Report must:

  • address the material areas under the agreed scope of services;
  • identify the legal and regulatory basis for material conclusions and recommendations;
  • provide a practical roadmap, indicative timeline, and cost assessment for each recommended or viable pathway, where applicable;
  • clearly distinguish confirmed information from assumptions, indicative estimates, and matters requiring further verification;
  • identify material legal, compliance, governance, operational, and implementation risks; and
  • be presented and discussed with RI management through the agreed consultation session.

RI Values

Guided by the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, as well as “Do No Harm,” Relief International Values:

  • Integrity
  • Adaptability
  • Collaboration
  • Inclusivity
  • Sustainability

As a humanitarian organization, Relief International is committed to the safeguarding of all those we come into contact with through our work. We are committed to the core humanitarian principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse. Relief International expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment and uphold the values and behaviors outlined in the Code of Conduct.

Recruitment to all roles in Relief International include a criminal records self-declaration, references, and other pre-employment checks, which may include police and qualifications checks.
